# THE RENEWAL
## of
# the Evangelical Spirit.

<note>The term "Evangelical" here refers to the "spirit of the Gospel" or living according to Christ's teachings, rather than the modern Protestant denomination.</note>

### FIRST PART.

<unclear>Which encompasses the deplorable state of Christians in these times, and the necessity of the reformation of their lives and their hearts.</unclear>

->BY<-

## ANTOINETTE BOURIGNON.

# T H E
## RENEWAL
## O F
## the Evangelical Spirit.

### FIRST PART.

*Which shows (by way of a private letter to a person who was following the impulses of their Corrupt Nature) the miseries and misfortunes that sin has brought to man; and how from such a beautiful and perfect Creature, made in the Likeness of God, he has become through sin so ugly, ignorant, powerless, and wretched in Body and Spirit.*

*This Treatise will also teach (primarily in its Second Part) the Method and the means by which man can die to this corruption, in order to live again in the <term>SPIRIT OF JESUS CHRIST</term> <note>original: "ESPRIT DE JESUS CHRIST." In Bourignon's theology, this refers to a literal internal transformation and a return to the purity of the early Christian church, rather than just an intellectual belief.</note>.*

->Composed by<-
->**ANTOINETTE BOURIGNON.**<-

### To the
# Children of God.

*In which are contained the great & fundamental Truths of the true Christian Religion: regarding the All of God, the Nothingness of Man <note>original: "le Tout de Dieu, le Neant de l'Homme." This reflects a core mystical concept where God is the only true reality, and the human ego, separated from God, is considered "nothing."</note>, his Freedom, his End, his Corruption, & his Renewal. We have cited in the margin several Passages from the Holy Scriptures to show the conformity of the Spirit of God with itself. However, we realized this strategy too late to be able to practice it throughout the rest of the book, which was already printed before this plan was conceived.*

<margin>**I.** *The design, subject matter, & necessity of this Work.*</margin>
I have proposed, CHILDREN OF GOD, to show you in this present treatise the state of a true Christian: what they must believe, what they must say & desire, & principally what they must practice to be a true Disciple of Jesus Christ. This is because all these things are so necessary in the present time that, <margin>*a* Psalm 119. v. 155.</margin> *a* unless one knows and practices them, there is no salvation to be hoped for. This is why I say and say again <margin>*b* Phil. 3. v. 1.</margin> *b* in various ways and with different terms the same things, in order to better instill them into the Heart & the Spirit of all those who desire to reach the blessed eternal life. And I find myself obliged to declare these Christian truths to you, since I see so many souls...

<vocab>Foreword, Children of God, Christian Religion, salvation, eternal life, Jesus Christ, Psalms, Philippians, design</vocab>

<keywords>Christian discipleship, spiritual practice, salvation, Antoinette Bourignon, biblical authority, the All of God, the Nothingness of Man, 17th-century mysticism</keywords>

And I have often remarked in persons of good will that after having noticed their faults, and wanting to correct them, they fell into even greater ones: so that their final faults were worse than the first. This cannot fail to happen, since the corruption of man increases as he commits faults and sins: and when he believes he is amending his faults and doing well through the movements of his *Corrupted Nature*, he falls into presumption of spirit, attributing to his corruption the power to do well, although it has no power except to do evil: which is an impotence <note>original: "impuissance"; here meaning a total lack of spiritual capacity or moral strength.</note>.

### MY DEAR READER,

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'T' inside a square border, containing a detailed landscape engraving of a building amidst trees.</image-desc>

Two types of people compel me to place at the beginning of all the books of Mademoiselle *Bourignon* <note>Antoinette Bourignon (1616–1680) was a Flemish mystic who claimed to receive direct revelations from God. Her radical ideas about personal spirituality led to frequent conflict with both Catholic and Protestant authorities.</note> the public Profession of her Faith and her Religion, which she openly presented to the Court of *Gottorp* in *Holstein* <note>The Duchy of Holstein-Gottorp, located in modern-day Germany. Bourignon fled there in 1671 seeking religious tolerance under Duke Christian Albrecht.</note>, and to join to it the Catalogue of those of her writings which are printed up to now. For since many rumors are spread almost everywhere to her disadvantage, many people (and almost all) believe them easily and without examination, especially when this comes from the clergy <note>Original: "gens d'Eglise." Bourignon's followers often used this term to critique the institutional hierarchy and the perceived arrogance of ordained ministers.</note>, whose word the people rely on, thinking that such Holy and Spiritual persons would not want to lie. Thus, they do not wish to take the trouble to inquire further whether what these Gentlemen claim against Mademoiselle *Bourignon* is true, nor to see the documents necessary to form a judgment of such consequence, upon which they often allow themselves to be carried away to actions that could well be the subject of eternal repentance. In order

therefore, so that these people who do not wish to take the trouble to inform themselves in detail of the Truth by reading the books of this Lady <note>Original: "Demoiselle." Antoinette Bourignon was often referred to by this title to denote her status as an unmarried woman of some social standing.</note>, might have the means to make a certain judgment of her, they will see here in five or six lines of her *Confession* the complete Summary and Foundation of all her Doctrine and her life, and will learn thereby not to believe so easily in public lies, invented even by Lutheran Priests <note>Bourignon faced significant opposition from Lutheran clergy during her time in Holstein and Hamburg, as her focus on "inner light" threatened their institutional authority.</note> and others, and peddled as much through their writings and books as through their words and their Preachings, through which they decry this person, her friends, and her Doctrine as impious, or as people of some new, wandering, and fantastical Religion <note>In the 17th century, "new" or "innovative" religions were viewed with deep suspicion and often equated with heresy or civil disorder.</note>, in order to fill the common people with horror. These people allow themselves to be turned away by this means from the knowledge of the saving Truth <note>Original: "Verité salutaire." Spiritual knowledge considered necessary for the salvation of the soul.</note> to the damage of their own souls, which they wound greatly by rash and false judgments and by strange passions to which these Slanderers <note>Original: "Calomniateurs."</note> dispose them, even to the point of often refusing the common duties of humanity to good people who seek only to please God.

But as there are still persons more composed and circumspect, who strive to regulate their judgments and their conduct by the specific knowledge of the Truth, if only they knew by what means to inform themselves; it is in their favor that I have joined the Catalogue of this Lady’s printed books, where I have marked in two or three words the principal matters of which they treat. I say nothing of her manuscripts, which are not yet printed, except that they will be when the occasion permits, and that being neither fewer in number,

nor inferior in dignity to those that have begun to appear, they all together cannot help but strike very strongly the hearts of well-disposed Readers, to make them return to their God. Nevertheless, permit me, Reader my dear Friend, that I warn you not to bring to their reading a spirit elevated like a Master or a Censor. <note>The author cautions against intellectual pride or a judgmental attitude, which were seen as barriers to spiritual enlightenment in mystical traditions.</note> God has no need for a Master, nor for the Wise. # PROFESSION
## OF
# FAITH & RELIGION,

->*Made publicly by*<-
->Miss ANTHOINETTE BOURIGNON.<-
<note>Antoinette Bourignon (1616–1680) was a Flemish mystic who gained a significant following across Europe. Because her teachings emphasized direct internal inspiration over church hierarchy, she was frequently accused of heresy; this document serves as her formal defense of her orthodoxy.</note>

->*On the doubts that one might have regarding her Belief*<-
->*& her Religion.*<-

->I.<-
I am a Christian; & I believe everything that a true Christian must believe.

->II.<-
I am baptized in the Catholic Church, in the Name of the Father, in the Name of the Son, in the Name of the Holy Spirit.

->III.<-
I believe the twelve Articles of the Creed, or the Apostles’ Creed; & do not doubt any Article thereof.

->IV.<-
I believe that Jesus Christ is true God, & that he is also true Man; And that he is the Savior & Redeemer of the World.

->V.<-
I believe in the Gospel; in the Holy Prophets; & in all of Holy Scripture, both the Old and the New Testament.

*And I wish to live & die in all the points of this Belief.*
*Which I protest <note>In this 17th-century context, "protest" means to solemnly declare or affirm before witnesses.</note> before God & men, to all those whom it may concern.*
*In witness whereof, I have signed this my Confession with my hand, & sealed it with my Seal. In Schleswig <note>Original: "Sleeswicq." This refers to the city in the Duchy of Schleswig (modern-day Germany), where Bourignon established a printing press during her exile.</note> the 11th of March 1675.*

<image-desc>A circular seal containing the letters "L. S." (Locum Sigilli) <note>Latin: "The place of the seal."</note>.</image-desc>

->*It was sealed, & signed below*<-

->*Anthoinette Bourignon.*<-

# CATALOGUE,

## Of the printed books composed by Miss Antoinette Bourignon, born in the City of Lille in Flanders.

->I.<-

The Light Born in Darkness, divided into four parts, which are full of salutary doctrines and instructions, both general and specific, as much Divine as moral, of Theory and of Practice, suited to opening the eyes and touching the hearts of men of good will, in order to dispose them to seek God and his truth, and to change their evil lives to embrace a new life according to God. *In French & in Flemish.* <note>Originally titled *La Lumière née en Ténèbres* (1669), this work is one of her most famous, focusing on the "inner light" and the corruption of the organized church.</note>

->II.<-

The Tomb of False Theology, exterminated by the True coming from the Holy Spirit. Divided into four parts. It treats several doctrinal matters that had mostly been proposed to Miss A. B. by way of opposition and to contradict her. There, one sees how the Sages, by means of their studies, have fallen away from the simple, solid, living, and effective truth of God, and from true Christian virtue; And that they have changed true Christianity into a disputatious and nitpicking Christianity, hypocritical and vicious, and such as the Church of Laodicea, <note>A reference to the Biblical "lukewarm" church in Revelation 3:14–22, which believed it was rich and needed nothing, but was actually "wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked."</note> unhappy, miserable, poor, blind, and naked: while it calls itself rich in virtue, and lacking in nothing regarding knowledge. *In French & Flemish.*

->III.<-

Innocence Recognized and Truth Discovered, etc. First part. Where one sees through a living example the hatred and cruelty that Priests themselves exercise upon their own Brothers who do not wish to condescend to their conduct, but rather to withdraw from the corruption of the world, making them then be betrayed, imprisoned, and suffer even unto death. *In French.* <note>This work, *L'Innocence reconnue*, is largely autobiographical and defensive, detailing the legal and religious persecutions Bourignon faced from the clergy.</note>

With a letter to a Father of the Oratory <note>The Oratorians are a Catholic society of apostolic life of priests and lay brothers; Bourignon frequently corresponded with various high-ranking clergy to defend her views.</note> on the same subject. *In French & Flemish.*

->IV.<-

The Light of the World. Divided into three parts, of which

### V.

*Warning against the Quakers* <note>original: "Advertiſſement contre les Trembleurs." In the 17th century, "Trembleurs" was the standard French term for the Religious Society of Friends, or Quakers.</note>, opposed to a defamatory pamphlet from this Sect against A. B. <note>Antoinette Bourignon.</note> Wherein it is shown that this Sect does not possess the light of the Holy Spirit, and in which their errors and fantasies are perfectly ruined. It is there proved solidly and thoroughly that one must obey, according to God, every kind of Magistrate and Superior, and that one must observe good regulations in the Political State, in the Ecclesiastical, and in common life. One also discovers there the qualities that a truly regenerated person, enlightened by God, must possess. ***In Flemish.***

### V I.

*The Testimony of Truth.* <note>original: "Le Teſmoignage de Verité."</note> Wherein are reported the public depositions of several persons worthy of trust concerning the life and conduct of the said Lady, whom they affirm under oath to have lived from her childhood in an extraordinarily virtuous and exemplary manner. Several other testimonies have also been added to confound the lies and calumnies that had been published against her person and her writings. It also treats how Christians have done wrong by creating divisions among themselves, using as a pretext certain irregularities in certain ceremonies and specific opinions that are non-essential to the Love of God, while they have exceeded in opposition and neglected their own regeneration and self-denial. <term>Item</term> <note>Latin for "likewise" or "also," commonly used in 17th-century lists to introduce a new point.</note>, concerning the true and false application of the merits of Jesus Christ. That the Commandments of God are not a burden, but the lovely effects of His Love and Paternal care; and that it is necessary, easy, and pleasant to observe them to be saved. Against personal <term>Predestination</term> <note>Bourignon strongly opposed the Calvinist doctrine that God has pre-chosen certain individuals for salvation or damnation regardless of their actions.</note>. Concerning the glorious Creation of Adam: of his fall, before which Jesus Christ took a body from him for Himself <note>Bourignon held unique mystical views on Adam's original nature, suggesting he was an androgynous being from whom Christ derived a spiritual body before the Fall.</note>; and of several other divine mysteries unknown until now. ***In German.*** <note>original: "En Alleman."</note>

# CATALOGUE.

## VII.

*Admirable Treatise on Solid Virtue. First Part.*
Wherein one sees that virtue must be learned through the gentleness and humility of Jesus Christ, which, by showing us our nothingness, causes us to mortify <note>The practice of "mortification" in 17th-century spirituality involved self-discipline and the "killing off" of worldly desires to focus on the spiritual life.</note> our corrupt nature in order to live again in the Love of God. One also discovers here all the artifices by which the Devil seeks to hinder and delay us in the progress of true virtue. *In French, Flemish, Latin, and German.*

## VIII.

*The Touchstone:* <note>A "touchstone" is a metaphor for a standard used to test the quality or genuineness of something, originally used to test precious metals.</note> Which shows how one must examine the validity of the Doctors and Guides of Souls, and that of their doctrines, upon the Touchstone of Charity or the Love of God. Therein one sees the refutation of the abominable lies and calumnies that were invented to provide a pretext for defaming and persecuting this Lady <note>Refers to Antoinette Bourignon herself.</note> to the death, as if she denied the Holy Trinity, the Eternal Divinity of Jesus Christ, His Holy merits, and as if she wished to overthrow the entire Christian Religion: and similar horrible falsehoods that have been imputed to her. Therein one also sees how and why God created man; what care He has taken to raise him from his fall; and how men are saved through the merits of Jesus Christ by observing His commandments. Also, concerning the decay of the Christian Church: and that God wishes to re-establish it on earth before the end of the world, and to begin this work of His from this moment forward. *In French, German, and Latin.*

## IX.

*Admirable Treatise on Solid Virtue: Second Part.*
Wherein it is shown that to reach true virtue one must: I. Abandon the world and no longer conform to it. II. Abandon covetousness, through a total mortification of corrupt Nature, by being content with simple necessity and with the least in all things. III. Abandon and renounce one’s own will—the great as much as the small, the unregenerate as much as the regenerate—and to fight against it until death, just as Jesus Christ himself did, coming to show us by his own person how, by following him and doing as he did, we may find the way out of our filth to be reunited with God. *In French and Flemish.*

# CATALOGUE.

## X.

*The Blindness of Men Today. First Part.* <note>original title: "L’Aveuglement des hommes de maintenant. Premiere Partie."</note> Apologetic Treatise on the occasion of the slanders spread against the behavior of Mlle. A. B. <note>The author, Antoinette Bourignon (1616–1680). Her works were often published under her initials to avoid immediate censorship.</note> Wherein one sees through living examples how corrupt nature blinds itself and is artful in concealing its flaws from itself and others, excusing and defending them by all kinds of pretexts, even those holy in appearance, not wishing to be rebuked, but rather casting them upon others and accusing others, while it does everything improperly, and even wishes to discharge itself from the duty of self-denial and change. All its pretexts are refuted here, and principally those it draws from the idea that Jesus Christ has done and suffered everything for men, and that they are too fragile to observe the commandments of God. *In French and Flemish.*

## XI.

*The Renewal of the Gospel Spirit. First Part.* <note>original title: "Le Renouvellement de l’Eſprit Evangelique. Premiere Partie."</note> Wherein the great and fundamental Truths of the true Christian Religion are proposed through divinely convincing and most extraordinary lights: of the All of God, of the Nothingness of man, of his Liberty, of the End of his Creation, of the Glory in which he was created, of the Miseries into which he has fallen, of his Corruption, of his Restoration, of the greatness of the Charity of Jesus Christ, and of that of His Merits by which He has redeemed men Three times from three great universal rebellions, coming to offer us now a third and final Redemption through the *Renewal of His Gospel Spirit:* And on this subject it is shown how deep is the incredible corruption of our nature and our wicked heart, and how necessary it is to fight and conquer them if one does not wish to be eternally damned. *In French, Flemish, Latin, and German.*

# R E A D E R .

*In this Divine Preface, the subject is the miseries into which man has fallen since the glorious state of his creation, described here; and how, through his affection for created things <note>Bourignon uses "creatures" to refer to anything created—people, objects, or worldly status—that distracts from the Creator.</note>, he has turned away from the purpose and the designs that God had in creating him; How everyone sustains one another in their evils and their vices through all sorts of pretexts, and above all by means of their Doctors <note>referring to academic theologians or "Doctors of the Church" whom she frequently criticized for intellectualizing faith</note>, even by persecuting the truth: How, notwithstanding this, the infinite goodness of God has not ceased to procure for them through Jesus Christ the means to recover their salvation, presenting to them at all times the medicine for their ills through His divine Laws, and especially in these latter times through His Evangelical Law <note>The "Law of the Gospel," or the core teachings of Christ</note> whose Spirit He wishes to renew; And how finally it is absolutely necessary to voluntarily embrace this Evangelical Law to be saved.*

# Preface.

<sig>A 2</sig>

But the greatest misfortune and the greatest deceptions existing in the world consist in the inner state of souls, which, far more than in regard to one’s civil state <note>meaning one's social standing or legal reputation in the eyes of the community</note>, mistake the false for the true and reality for appearance.

<margin>4. These [deceptions] are unknown to those of good will.</margin>
And although this spiritual deception is more dangerous and harmful, yet it is less known and little considered. Men of good will now live in a false peace regarding their salvation, because their lives have the appearance of goodness and virtue. And this is so artfully disguised that they themselves believe they are living well and being virtuous, when in fact all their words and actions are continual sins: For being born in sin and inclined toward all sorts of evils, they live within this inclination and fall insensibly from one sin to another without believing they are doing wrong. As long as their actions are not reprehensible before men, they believe themselves to be in a good state and presume their salvation to be infallible—all the more so since other men judge them to be in the grace of God and in a state of salvation for not harming anyone, not lying, committing adultery, or stealing. Moreover, beyond ceasing to commit these types of evils, they also perform many kinds of good deeds, in their own view and according to the judgment of men: For they call themselves Christians, they go to churches, receive the Sacraments <term>Sacraments</term> <note>religious rites such as the Eucharist or Confession, seen as channels of divine grace</note>, give from their excess to the poor, speak willingly of virtue and spiritual things, converse with good people like themselves, despise the worldly and the fraudulent, and avoid their company as much as possible; in short, they do everything on the outside that a good Christian ought to do.

<margin>5. Discovered, but too late, at the hour of death.</margin>

<margin>8. Their assurance of salvation is deceptive and false.</margin>
And in this wretched state, men dare to await death and live in peace regarding their salvation: which is the greatest deception of all. For those who recognize their misfortune, and how far they are from God and His Truth, can seek the means to draw closer to Him and to recover the truth; but those who believe they already possess these things will do nothing to obtain or find them again, but will instead die in a miserable lethargy that will insensibly lead them to hell, contrary to their intentions and the presumption of their salvation, which they falsely promise themselves; since no one can be saved unless he attains the end <note>The "end" refers to the *telos* or ultimate purpose for which a human being exists.</note> for which he was created, which is none other than to *love his God with all his heart, and with all his strength, and with all his thoughts.* <note>A reference to the Great Commandment found in Luke 10:27 and Deuteronomy 6:5.</note>

<margin>9. Turning away from the purpose of their Creation.</margin>
See, Friend Reader, if the men of today live in this Love and do that for which they were created; and judge if they can truly be saved by living and dying in the manner we see them live and die. For my part, I can see nothing else except that everyone is walking along *the wide path that Jesus Christ told us leads to perdition* <note>original: "le chemin large... qu'il meine à perdition" referring to Matthew 7:13.</note>; since all their affections are divided into as many subjects as there are different objects that they love. But His good pleasure was to create a man in His likeness in order to take His delight with him; and as there can be no perfect love unless it is reciprocal, God willed that man should love his God with all his power in return for the love that God bore for him; and that he should have delighted in Him alone, since God wished to delight in him and take His pleasure with man: which obligated man to place all his affections in God alone. Since he was created for no other end, he neither could nor should in justice turn his affections toward anything other than toward his God, to love Him uniquely with all his strength and all his power.

...[those things they] esteem or honor, and fail to see that they themselves are far greater **idolaters** than those who worship idols made of some metal. For it is to be believed that **Christians** have more affection for their riches, honors, and the pleasures of taste and the flesh, than these **Pagans** have for their cast idols. To those idols, the Pagans cannot attach their hearts as much as these so-called Christians attach theirs to their own **self-love**—an object of such idolatry that they forget God for its sake. Whereas these Pagans still know God and remember Him, confessing that there is a God who is the Author of all things, many Christians instead deny that there is a God by their deeds. And though they confess Him with their mouths, they are liars in their words, since their deeds destroy their speech.

<margin>12. Proofs of this effective atheism.</margin>
And I would gladly ask many of these Christians: how could they live any worse if there were no God? For in truth, they commit every evil they can in secret, and whenever they do not fear human reprimand. If there were indeed no God, they would still not wish to be blamed by other men; therefore, they would not commit any greater evils even if there were no God to punish them <note>The author argues that social pressure, rather than fear of God, is the only thing restraining people from greater sin.</note>. They give free rein to the inclinations of their **corrupt nature**, which, being born in sin, leans toward every kind of evil. They follow these impulses without even thinking they do wrong, because sin so blinds their souls that they no longer see or think of God, nor of eternal things. These matters are as unknown to them as they are invisible, for they no longer see anything with their understanding except earthly and visible things.

<margin>13. Christians think only of this earthly life.</margin>
Consequently, one should rather call the men of today by a more fitting and descriptive name: "**earthlings**" <note>original: "terriens". The author is making a phonetic and conceptual contrast between "Chrétiens" (Christians) and "terriens" (those of the earth).</note> rather than Christians, seeing as they do not think [of anything but the world]...

# Preface.

...[they] neither speak, nor work, nor study, nor do anything for the duration of their lives except for the sake of the earth and for time <note>original: "la terre & le temps" — referring to material possessions and the temporary nature of mortal life</note>, or to try to make themselves comfortable and happy in this miserable life, as if man were created only for it; this they do even though all men have come here only to perform **penance** <term>penance: an act of devotion or self-discipline to show sorrow for sin</term> and to work toward recovering the **Love of God** which all men lost in **Adam** through his sin.

<margin>14. *This is a life of penance, and not our primary purpose.*</margin>
Consequently, men should do nothing in this world that does not aim at this single purpose, since they are sent here for this reason alone. Human judgment can understand this by seeing that no men do anything here but eat and drink, sleep, and work for the maintenance of their **mortal life**; they are born in suffering and die in distress. Since all these things are bad, they cannot have been created by God, and even less can they have been the end or the goal for which God created man. It is a necessity that God must have had another purpose in creating man than these **temporal** and fleeting things, which cause man so many evils and miseries—nearly unbearable for many.

<margin>15. *Miseries of this life and of nature. They do not come from God.*</margin>
Such things cannot come from a God who is all-good and all-perfect, who can do nothing but good; for all His works are without any mixture of evil, being all good and all perfect, just as their Author is, who can never do wrong. All the **evils** we see in **nature**, both general and specific, have emerged from sin. This sin, having forced its way into the works of God, has corrupted and spoiled all the things that God had made very good. For after having created fire with a sweet and temperate heat to pleasantly warm all of nature, sin brought to it the burning heat and the smoke, which are two bad things that God did not create. For it was necessary that everything subject to man should be subject with him to the curse he had drawn upon himself; and that everything given to him for his nourishment and delight should instead serve him with pain and sadness. Thus, the order of things changed, because man had changed the order that God had established within him: namely, to Love God alone with all his power.

<margin>19. How miserable he has become.</margin>

<margin>34. Necessity of dying to corruption to be reborn.</margin>

For these two Spirits are two opposites that drive each other out and cannot remain [together].

<margin>51. Why were the Laws not given to the Ancients?</margin>

This was a far heavier fault than the one into which they had all fallen through the sin of Adam, because the individual will of every person had actively committed evil, whereas previously they had only sinned through the will of Adam without their own cooperation. This obliged Jesus Christ to perform more duties to redeem men this second time than He had done the first; for the first time, He had only a single will <note>the will of Adam as the representative of humanity</note> to conquer and submit to the will of God to return it to grace. But now, so many hundreds of millions of diverse wills had rebelled against the will of God to follow their own desires. It then required as many specific warnings and teachings as there were men fallen into various sins, providing them with as many different means to return to grace as there were ways they had lost it through various kinds of sins by fixing their affections on different objects.

This signifies nothing other than the promise he made that his Gospel will remain until the end of the world; and though many would fight against it, his enemies will never submerge it; it will always remain in its integrity for those who wish to follow and observe it. 

But the wicked, who have wanted to shake from their shoulders the yoke of the Gospel Law <note>The "Law of the Gospel" refers to the teachings of Christ, which the author views as a mandatory set of rules for living.</note> to follow their own corrupt natures, have drawn arguments from this very law suited to their own laxity. By this means, they confuse the minds of the ignorant, who, not knowing how to discern the truth, have easily followed error and lies when these were covered with a veneer of piety and holiness. 

And by this means, several sects and religions <note>In this context, "religions" refers to specific denominations or religious orders rather than different world faiths.</note> have entered into the Church of God, and have so far progressed for the worse that one no longer knows where to find the truth. This is because each of these sects claims to possess it, even though all of them in general, and each of them in particular, have fallen away from the true sense of Gospel doctrine. They possess nothing more than the interpretations that each has pulled from it in their own fashion, and according to their desire to live at their ease. 

The result is that the true Gospel doctrine is no longer observed anywhere, even though everyone wants to claim the name of doing so and of being a Christian—especially those who believe themselves to be reformed <note>A reference to the "Reformed" or Protestant churches.</note>. And all these things, with many others, Jesus Christ came to teach to men, to show them the means by which they could recover the LOVE OF GOD which they had lost through ignorance, or by thinking it was permitted for them to enjoy all these things agreeable to their senses without offending God, since he had created them for man. This would have been true if man had remained faithful in the LOVE of his God: he would then have been able to enjoy with delight all that is beautiful and good in all of nature. But the frailty he contracted through sin forbids him from doing this, since he does not know how to love all these things, nor any of them, without withdrawing his affections from his God as he moves to love these <term>creatures</term> <note>In 17th-century theological French, "creatures" refers to any created thing—whether objects, physical pleasures, or other people—as opposed to the Creator.</note>. This is why it is absolutely necessary to stop loving them if one wishes to return to the Love of one's God: which Jesus Christ came to make known to them as much by his teachings as by his practices. It is not that God has need of our poverty, humility, abstinence, or other of our virtues, since he is in himself all-rich, all-good, and perfect without the intervention of men; but they have great need of using these means to recover the LOVE OF GOD, outside of which there is no salvation.

<margin>103 Christ’s atonement does not exclude the efforts of men.</margin>
This is why Jesus Christ came at the final hour to redeem humanity a second time when he was born into this mortal world: to present them with the means for their salvation. He did not come to redeem them in the manner that these <term>Glossers<note>From the French *glosseurs*, referring to scriptural commentators or theologians who provide "glosses" (interpretations) that the author believes distort the plain meaning of the text.</note></term> teach—claiming that he paid and <term>satisfied<note>Theological "satisfaction" refers to the idea of Christ paying the debt of human sin to divine justice.</note></term> everything for humanity without them needing to do anything themselves. This contradicts the entire Old and New Testaments, where God has so many times said to men through his ancient Prophets: *If you keep my commandments, and you do this or that, I will give you such and such a blessing; but if you do not do what I command you, I will give you the curse of such and such punishments.* And in the New Testament, is it not written, as I have already cited: *According to your works you shall be judged, and according to your works you shall be condemned.*? And does Jesus Christ not say: *He who wants to come after me, let him renounce himself, let him take up his cross and follow me?* And elsewhere Jesus Christ says: *That he has done all his works to give us an example*, along with so many other passages with which Scripture is filled, to teach men that they must themselves put their hands to the work, and *work out their salvation with fear and trembling; that it is necessary to watch, and always pray, and never cease.* Whereas these Glossers of the Scriptures say that men should do nothing, and that Jesus Christ has satisfied everything for them.

<margin>104 Christ's merits provide no benefit outside the practice of his Laws.</margin>
I wish to leave everyone free to believe in God or in men (of whom Scripture says, they are all liars): For after I have declared to them through this present treatise the truths that God makes known to me, I have fulfilled my part, and I have no interest in their salvation or their damnation. And God has even less. <note>The author suggests that God is not personally diminished by human failure, emphasizing that the consequences of sin fall entirely upon the individual.</note> Everyone must "make their bed as they wish to sleep" <note>A traditional idiom (original: *un chacun doit faire son lict comme il veut coucher*) meaning one must live with the consequences of one's own choices.</note>, to use the graces that God presents to them now, or to reject them; for all the good and the evil that will happen from it...

They boast of having the Gospel and Faith in Jesus Christ, although by their works they deny that same Faith. <margin>112. They cannot deceive like others.</margin>
And you may well believe, my Dear Reader, that in doing this no one can be deceived, since God never deceives. All Christians must know this Law, since the Gospel has remained in writing in their hands, according to the promise that Jesus Christ made, *that he would be with them until the end of the world.*

# Preface.

[...the] Gospel <note>The text continues from the previous page: "But Christian [teachings are a] Gospel..."</note> which aims solely at recovering the Love of God, which is the **Charity** <term>Charity<note>From the Latin *caritas*; in this spiritual context, it refers not to almsgiving, but to the supreme theological virtue of selfless, divine love for God and neighbor.</note></term> of which St. Paul spoke, without which no one has been able, nor will be able in the future, to be saved. Even if one possessed all the other virtues together, it would be nothing without **Charity**; and he who has **Charity** alone possesses within himself all the other virtues, and cannot perish even if he were not to observe to the letter all the other circumstances of the things contained in the <term>Gospel Law<note>The "New Law" of the New Testament, contrasted here with the "Old Law" of legalistic rituals.</note></term>. It is observance enough to possess true **Charity** in one's soul, since that is the end for which God created man, and nothing other than his Love will ever be asked of man on the part of God.

But man, for his own part, has need of the observance of all the particulars of this Gospel Law, since he has transgressed the Law of the Love of God through so many different objects that he has loved instead of his God, which he must absolutely abandon if he wishes to return to His Love; since one cannot at the same time have one’s affections set upon two objects so different as are perishable things compared to an Eternal God. And it is of necessity that he who loves God must cease to love any earthly things; and he who loves the goods of this world must cease to love God.

<margin>115. *True and false conversion.*</margin>
And this is the certain mark by which to know if a person is truly converted or not. For as long as they still have their affections for anything fleeting, they cannot have them in God. To believe so is to deceive oneself, and to say so is to deceive others. By this, one can easily discover that these changes of Religion cannot bring salvation, even if one were to run from one Religion to another every day of one’s life, and create new sects every day, and follow false or true Prophets. All this will do nothing for our salvation if in effect we do not practice the Law

<margin>116. Known Truth. Persecution of A.B. <note>A.B. refers to the author, Antoinette Bourignon (1616–1680). She was a prominent mystic who claimed to receive direct revelations from God, leading to significant conflict with both Catholic and Protestant authorities.</note></margin>

At this I should not be astonished: since they treated Jesus Christ their Savior in this way, they may well do the same to his creature. And this does not afflict me, since Jesus Christ said,

<margin>118. Universal Grace.</margin>
No one must excuse themselves from it, since this grace is universal for all men, just as it was also for the sin of Adam, and for the particular sins of all men when Jesus Christ came to redeem them by taking on their mortality: given that God has never had and will never have any partiality. He has chosen all those who wish to love him, and rejects all those who wish to place their affections on transitory things.

Everything else commented upon in another way are errors and inventions of corrupt men, who, to flatter their sins, say that nothing happens without the foreknowledge of God, so that their failings <note>original: "relafchemens." This they also do regarding their neglect of doing good. They say that God does not give them the grace for it, and that they could do nothing well of themselves while feeling inclined toward all evils.

For when God, through His Law, forbade the eating of pork, or other fats or unclean animals, it was only to master their gluttony <note>Original: "friandises," meaning delicacies or a lack of restraint regarding food.</note>. Likewise, they were not to eat two kinds of food with their bread, such as meat and butter, or butter with cheese <note>Bourignon interprets the Mosaic dietary restrictions (specifically the prohibition of mixing meat and dairy) as spiritual exercises in self-discipline rather than merely arbitrary rules.</note>. <margin>

for men,

Instead, the people of that time needed to observe all these things to return to the **LOVE OF GOD** which they had lost through as many different means as God gave them different Laws. It happened in exactly the same way when the Gospel Law was given. It is not that God is concerned with whether men are rich or poor when He ordains **poverty of spirit** <note>A spiritual state of humility and detachment from worldly possessions, regardless of one's actual wealth.</note>; and God also has no need for us to renounce ourselves or carry the cross to follow Jesus Christ, since—

<margin>157 Use without affection.</margin>
One might perhaps tell me that it is necessary to love oneself for preservation, and that one must use other creatures for necessity: which I admit. But there is a great difference between *using* and *bestowing affection*. God has given life to man, and it must be preserved. He also created so many diverse creatures for the nourishment and necessity of man: but He wished to reserve the heart and the affections entirely for Himself alone. That is why one may certainly use all these things, but one cannot bestow affection upon them: since this affection of the heart is reserved by God. Just as He gave freedom to Adam to eat of all the fruits of the earthly Paradise, except for that of a single tree, of which he was not to eat; so too is it permitted to use drink, food, land, clothing, and every other thing necessary for life: but it is not permitted to fix one's heart there, or to place one's affections there: since that is the fruit...

# THE RENEWAL

# THE GOSPEL SPIRIT.
## *Part One.*

To show the necessity of being renewed by the Gospel Spirit, it is demonstrated here how great the corruption of our nature is. This corruption appears in all its behaviors, in the thoughts, judgments, and opinions it holds of itself—following only its own will and the profound deception of the human heart. The heart misunderstands itself in everything, believing it loves God and is virtuous when it only seeks to satisfy the inclinations and pleasures of its corrupt nature <note>The concept of "corrupt nature" (la nature corrompue) is central to 17th-century spiritual writing, referring to the state of humanity after the Fall, driven by self-love rather than love for God.</note>. To this end, even the scholars <note>original: "doctes." This refers to the theologians and university-educated intellectuals of the time, whom the author often accused of intellectualizing faith to avoid true sacrifice.</note> of today have adapted their doctrines, perverting the Law of Jesus Christ. One must follow this Law by mortifying the flesh and its lusts, even if one only wished to lessen their damnation, but how much more so to be Saved by the **RENEWAL OF THE GOSPEL SPIRIT**? The reader should consider their own person while reading this letter, rather than the individual to whom it was originally written; because, undoubtedly, everyone will find within themselves all too much of this same corruption in substance, and perhaps even more.

### VII.

<margin>
VIII.
Dispositions for becoming a Christian, contrary to corrupt nature.
</margin>

### VIII.

But the person who wishes to become a Christian is sensitive only to things concerning the perfection of their soul; they value and esteem all the means that lead to this perfection, and care very little whether they perform a lowly <note>original: "vile"—at the time, this referred to "low-status" manual labor, like cleaning or cooking, rather than something morally wicked.</note> or honorable duty, provided that they please God. But the purely natural man acts just like a beast, which, being put in a meadow, looks only for the best grass or pasture. In the same way, the natural person also acts when they change location; they focus on or consider whether they are well-housed and well-treated; if they are well-bedded there and provided with everything; if they have food <note>original: "viandes"—a general term for food or sustenance, not exclusively animal flesh.</note> and drink to their taste, etc.

For this reason, the Christian soul is always content with simple necessity, and does not wish (even when it is able) to taste the delights of the present life, so as to wait to taste them in the next for all Eternity.

Man can resist the works of his corruption and destroy them.

It is true that a person can do no good on their own, being inclined toward all evils, and that all good comes from God alone. But they can, nevertheless, resist the evil that they themselves commit. For God did not create the corruption of human nature; it is a work of man himself, who should have as much power over his own handiwork as a painter or artisan has over some image or figure he has formed. He can break or shatter it according to his will, since the material belongs to him as much as the craftsmanship. He can throw it into the fire, or otherwise annul it, when it is disagreeable to him. # Part I. The Evangelical Spirit.

...to all souls who are submitted and abandoned to him.

<margin>XXXI. Why the Holy Spirit does not lead all souls or communicate himself to them.</margin>
But he leaves you in all these faults since you wish to rule yourself; and rightly so, since the Holy Spirit forces no one and only imparts his graces to those who seek and desire them by surrendering themselves entirely to him. For he would bestow graces in vain on those who are not disposed to follow his teachings. Therefore, it is no wonder that so few people have dealings with God and receive the <term>wisdom</term> <note>original: "sapience" — a term derived from Latin typically used in spiritual literature to denote a higher, divinely-inspired wisdom rather than mere human intelligence.</note> of his Holy Spirit, since so few are found who have this hunger and thirst for <term>Righteousness</term> <note>original: "Justice" — in the context of the 17th century and the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:6), this refers to "righteousness" or moral and spiritual uprightness.</note>, and even fewer who entirely abandon their own wills to his guidance. For usually, people prefer to do wrong by following their own **Wills** than to do right by following the **Will of God**, which alone is good.

<margin>XXXII. God does not compel the fulfillment of the good desires he gives. The increase of grace.</margin>
And since God wanted man to be a completely free creature, he lets him act according to his liberty, which will never be forced to do either good or evil, since these two things depend on the choice the person makes. The good Spirit indeed gives him good desires and light to discern good from evil; but this Holy Spirit will never constrain the **Will** of man, who, by listening to his good impulses and putting them into practice, will always receive a subsequent increase of graces. This is what the **Scripture** confirms...

### Part I. The Evangelical Spirit.

...worthy, having rendered himself incapable of inheriting the great wealth of a Father whom he has so offended; for it would not be just that a **Prodigal Child** <note>original: "Enfant prodigue"; a reference to the biblical Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15), who squanders his inheritance on a dissolute life</note> and debauchee should inherit the goods that his Father acquired for him with such care. It is a matter of **Justice** that such a Father restrains such a Child, and does not give him the liberty to dispose of the Father’s goods, even though by nature they would have been legitimately his. It is necessary for the Child’s own good that he be deprived of this liberty, since he would abuse it to his own harm. 

Thus God restrains <term>nature corrompue; the human state after the Fall, inclined toward sin rather than God</term>, and does not want it to enjoy or dispose of everything beautiful and good that He created for man; rather, he wishes that nature should humble itself and consider itself unworthy of even the things necessary for its upkeep. This is far from tasting and enjoying the beautiful and good things that God created for His Children, and not for the wicked, or those who abuse His graces.

<margin>
LVI. *Deceptions of the human heart, believing that everything beautiful and good is for him.*
</margin>

In this, many are mistaken by saying that God created for them everything beautiful and good in nature: for this is false, and they can enjoy nothing beautiful or good except in the way that **thieves** <note>original: "larrons"; the author implies that using God's creations without a right relationship with Him is a form of spiritual theft</note> enjoy the goods they have stolen from another. Thus, the wicked enjoy with iniquity good meats, fine clothes and ornaments, and all other delicious things that God created for His beloved alone—and not for people who set their affections on such vile things, loving them as if they were the ultimate ends for which they were created, even though they say in words that they receive them with **thanksgivings** <note>original: "actions de graces"; formal prayers of thanks, which the author suggests are hollow if the heart is not truly aligned with God</note>.

<margin>LVII. *Deceptions of the heart believing it makes use of beauty and goodness while offering thanks to God.*</margin>

This is just as false as the other deceptions: for they cannot truly have thanks to render to God for things they believe they deserve as their own property, or as things God created specifically for them. It is to be believed that the delight they take in taste or in sensual satisfactions effectively prevents them from lifting their hearts to God to thank Him for the beautiful and good things He gives them. Instead, they act like the **swine** <note>original: "pourceau"; the comparison of a thankless person to a pig eating acorns without looking up at the tree was a popular moralizing image in the 17th century</note> beneath an **oak tree** eating the acorns that are shaken down for it; it is more concerned with seeking them out and gorging itself than with looking up at the one who makes them fall. 

The sensual person does exactly the same regarding God when tasting delicacies or other delightful things: they are more concerned with gorging themselves and satisfying their appetites than with thanking God. Indeed, God is far from the memory of those who have fixed their affections outside of Him. For Scripture tells us that *where your heart is, there is your treasure* <note>original: "là où est vostre cœur, là est vostre thresor"; a reference to Matthew 6:21</note>; this shows that for those who have placed their affections in eating and drinking, or in other sensualities, there lies their heart and their treasure. And if such a person speaks of God, it is only from the **tips of the lips** <note>original: "du bout des levres"; an idiom meaning insincerely or superficially</note>, since the heart cannot be divided between affections for objects so different and distant from one another.

<margin>*LVIII. Mortification and suffering, the only path to salvation.*</margin>

These souls denied themselves the slightest sensual pleasure, "circumcising their flesh" for the Kingdom of Heaven, as have all those who have been saved until now, and as all will do until the end of the world. For there will never be any other path to salvation than the cross and the sufferings of Jesus Christ. This is where the proverb says, *For one pleasure, a thousand pains*: for in truth, I have never seen a pleasure in this world that did not end in pain or displeasure. 

And although this is experienced by many, they still wish to follow and taste these things to the detriment of eternal life. They persuade themselves they will have this eternal life in the end, after having tried to satisfy the five senses of their corrupt nature and having taken as much ease and pleasure in this world as they could. In this, they are greatly mistaken, since the Justice of God gives and will always give to each one according to their works. For this reason, the Scripture says, *according to your works you shall be judged, and according to your works you shall be condemned.* It does not say "according to your imaginations" or "strong hopes," or according to the belief one has imagined of having two Paradises: one in this world by seeking its delights, and the other in the Kingdom of Heaven, where nevertheless *nothing defiled enters.* Instead, each person shall be presented at the judgment of God, where it will be said: *behold the man and his works.*

Deceptions of the heart, which believes it does not sin while taking its ease.

I know well that many imagine (as you also do, my friend) that it is not an evil deed to follow one's appetites in eating and drinking, taking one's ease and comforts, or other satisfactions of nature. This is exactly what this wealthy man had done, of whom the Scripture says: *that he feasted sumptuously and clothed himself in purple and fine linen.* See here all the crimes of which the Scripture accuses him, without any other sin.

This ought to truly prevent one from believing that they will not be damned for having feasted well <note>original: "faisoit bonne chere"; to live luxuriously or eat well</note>, or for having dressed pompously and in fine linen, as is normally done by all those who are provided with the goods of fortune. L X I.
*As many kinds of Eternal torments as there are kinds of temporal pleasures.*
</margin>

This is further confirmed in the Scriptures when they speak of the Great Harlot <note>original: "grande Paillarde"; a reference to the Whore of Babylon in the Book of Revelation, symbolizing worldly corruption and idolatry</note>, saying: *give her as much torment as she has taken pleasure in her delights.* For my part, I hold that a person will have throughout all Eternity as many kinds of torments as they have delighted in various kinds of pleasures. Catholics illustrate this in a book entitled **THE ART OF LIVING WELL AND DYING WELL** <note>original: "L'ART DE BIEN VIVRE ET DE BIEN MOURIR"; a famous late-medieval and early modern devotional text (Ars moriendi) that used woodcut illustrations to teach the faithful how to resist temptation</note>, where the various torments suffered by damned souls in hell are represented through paintings.

It is depicted there that the gluttonous and the greedy <term>friands & gourmands</term> <note>terms describing those who seek out delicate, expensive delicacies and those who eat to excess</note> will be served at their tables with serpents, lizards, toads, spiders, and other venomous beasts, which the Devils will force into their mouths, pouring molten lead and cups of venom down their throats. And for the lustful <term>luxurieux</term>, there is a painting showing people entirely naked, to whom several serpents are attached, biting and gnawing at their genital parts, entering and exiting their bellies which they have torn open and from which they have pulled the entrails. <margin>LXII. Good & evil rewarded eternally in proportion.</margin>
God will leave no evil unpunished, nor any good without reward. For in proportion to the charity & Love of God found in a soul, so will that soul be raised to various degrees of glory. This is also verified by the Scripture, when it says,
> *In my Father’s house there are many mansions:* <note>original: "En la maison de mon Pere il y a diverses demeures"; a reference to John 14:2</note>
that is to say, that there will be in Paradise as many degrees of glory as the person possessed virtue in this world; and the one who imitated Jesus Christ most closely in this world will approach Jesus Christ most closely for all Eternity in his glory. This is why one must consider themselves happier to carry their cross, and be despised with Jesus Christ, than to have riches to live at ease and enjoy themselves in this short & miserable life, since this temporal Paradise cannot have, in all its delights, even the smallest joy and contentment that will be found in the blessed eternal life.

<margin>
LXIII.
Those who seek their delights here find pleasures neither in this world, nor in the next.
</margin>

This is good to understand by establishing as an eternal truth that there are no true goods except in God alone, and that there can be no greater evil than the deprivation of all good. It is to this deprivation that all those die who wish to take their delights in this world, to whom God will say: *Depart from me, all you who work iniquity* <note>original: "Retirez vous de moy vous tous qui faites iniquité"; a reference to Matthew 7:23</note>; or this sentence: *Go, you accursed, into eternal fire* <note>original: "Allez maudits au feu eternel"; a reference to Matthew 25:41</note>. He thus sends away from Him all those who wanted to take their delights in something other than God alone—the very purpose for which they had been created by Him. 

But sensual men <note>referring to people who are governed by their physical senses and worldly desires rather than spiritual concerns</note> are only sensitive to present things, without understanding anything of the blessed Eternity for which they were created, and for nothing else. They prefer a small, fleeting sensual pleasure to eternal delights which will never end. And in this way, they will have no Paradise either in this world, nor in the one to come. For even if one seeks perfect contentment in this world, it will never be found, since our souls, being divine <note>the author suggests the soul is "divine" because it is created in God's image and designed for communion with Him</note>, can be satisfied by God alone. By not having sought eternal delights in this world, they will never find them; at death, they find themselves deprived of both Paradises <note>meaning they lose both the spiritual peace possible on earth and the glory of heaven</note>, being no longer able to enjoy the temporal pleasures for which they nonetheless lost eternal pleasures.

**LXVII.**
*One must abstain from the pleasures of this life so as not to be so severely damned. How much more so to be saved?*
</margin>

Therefore, a person is very ill-advised to take their sensual pleasures here, tasting them as much as they can: since they must bear the pains of Hell in proportion to how much they enjoyed the pleasures of their five natural senses in this world. This is what Scripture affirms in the words previously cited concerning the Harlot <note>original: "la Paillarde." This is a reference to the "Whore of Babylon" in the Book of Revelation (18:7), where the text says: "As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so give her a like measure of torment and mourning."</note>, of whom it says: **give her as much torment as she had pleasures in this world**. Consequently, even a wicked person should wean themselves from the pleasures of this life so as not to increase their pains in the Hells <note>The author uses the plural "Hells" (Enfers), a common theological phrasing in the 17th century to describe the various degrees or regions of punishment.</note>; and they should cease to sin even if they knew they were to be damned, so that they might lessen the pains they must suffer in the Hells according to whether they committed few or many sins in this world. How much more must one abstain from sin altogether to possess Eternal Life, and to absolutely avoid this Hell?

<margin>
**LXVIII.**
*One must decide either to be damned by following one’s corrupted nature, or to be saved by fighting against it.*
</margin>

I think, my friend, that you can see by this letter how much the nature of man has been corrupted by sin; and that one cannot follow this corruption without damning one’s soul; and that one also cannot be saved without warring against and conquering this corruption, which is an enemy of God; and that the person who chooses their Paradise in this world by seeking their ease and pleasures here is cruel to themselves and an enemy of their own well-being. It is now for you to know whether you wish to persevere in following your corrupted nature (as you have done until now;)

It is now that the saving Grace of God appears clearly to all men; She <note>In French, "Grace" is a feminine noun, and Bourignon personifies it here as a guiding maternal or disciplinary figure.</note> who submits us like children to her discipline and her correction to make us renounce all that does not belong to true piety—the affections and the lusts of this world—so that we may live with temperance, with justice, and with piety in this present age <note>original: "siecle present" — referring to the temporal, worldly era as opposed to eternity.</note> which passes in a moment, while we are in the hope of an eternal Felicity, and of the manifestation of the glory of **JESUS CHRIST**, this Great God, who is Our Savior; who gave himself for us in order to redeem us fully from the slavery of disobedience to the Law of God, and to purge us to be for him a People of his own, who study nothing more than the practice of good.

### 1st Epistle of St. John, ch. III, vs. 1, 2, 3.

## TO THE READER.

I fear, **D E A R  R E A D E R**, that you might find cause for astonishment that, in wishing to speak of the RENEWAL OF THE EVANGELICAL SPIRIT, I have expanded so much upon the corruption that sin has brought into man, and also upon the glory and the noble state in which man was created. Know that I have done this with mature deliberation, so as to provide very powerful motives for embracing the *Evangelical Life* <note>In Bourignon’s context, "Evangelical" refers strictly to the teachings of the four Gospels (the *Evangelium*) rather than a specific Protestant denomination.</note>. For what use would it be to show you the means of practicing an *Evangelical Life* before you have a resolution strong enough to embrace it? For if the fear of Hell or the delights of Paradise do not induce you to an *Evangelical Life*, [human] nature will never embrace it: since this Evangelical Law is entirely repugnant to that Law of corrupt nature, which, knowing it has only this mortal life to last, takes as much pleasure and contentment as it can, having nothing else to hope for in the future, being like a dead beast, which is completely finished by this death. Therefore, one must never consult this corrupt nature in order to do good, or to follow and love eternal things, wherein corruption will never have any part. It is only the soul and the reason of man that can love these things, and renounce self <note>Original: "renoncer à ſoymeſme" (to renounce oneself), a core concept in 17th-century mysticism involving the suppression of the ego to make room for God.</note> to follow an *Evangelical Life*. This is why I wanted, above all, to speak of eternal glory to move hearts to love and seek it, so that with a great heart one may overcome all the difficulties that might be encountered in the search for this Evangelical Pearl of so great a price <note>A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" in Matthew 13:45-46, symbolizing the Kingdom of Heaven.</note>.

<vocab>Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit, corruption, sin, Evangelical Life, Hell, Paradise, Law of nature, Evangelical Pearl</vocab>

<summary>Antoinette Bourignon addresses her readers to explain why she must first describe the "corruption" of humanity before teaching the "Evangelical Life." She argues that since the Gospel contradicts our fallen instincts, a person must be motivated by the hope of eternal glory to overcome natural selfishness.</summary>
<keywords>Antoinette Bourignon, Evangelical Life, original sin, human nature, spiritual motivation, Pearl of Great Price, self-denial</keywords>

--- Page 334 ---
<meta>This page continues the preface "To the Reader." Having established that human nature is corrupt and must be overcome, Bourignon here explains that either the fear of damnation or the hope of heaven is a valid starting point for the spiritual journey, provided they lead to the "hatred of oneself" necessary for divine love.</meta>

### TO THE READER.

For it seems to me that there is no more powerful motive to move the heart of man than the hope of eternal happiness. The fear of the torments of Hell can also move some hardened hearts. It matters not <note>Original: "C’est tout un," an idiom meaning it is all the same or of equal value.</note> by what means one comes to love Eternal Life, whether through fear or through hope, provided that one arrives at this Love and at the hatred of oneself, since the one cannot go without the other. If one loves oneself and this present life, one cannot love God nor Eternity. Hold fast to this lesson, Dear Reader: and when I see someone who is truly resolved to renounce themselves <note>To "renounce oneself" (renoncer à ſoymeſme) is the mystical practice of abandoning one's own ego and desires to be guided solely by God.</note> and to embrace an *Evangelical Life*, I will show in the *Third Part* the true method for leading an *Evangelical Life* in order to be a Child of God and an heir to Heaven. In the meantime, receive with favor this *Second Part*, which will be useful and salutary if you examine it closely with attention. Of this, she who remains assures you,

->DEAR READER,<-

->*Your well-affectioned in*<-
->*Jesus Christ,*<-

->ANTOINETTE BOURIGNON.<-

**XCIX.** Man has fallen out of harmony with the *Goodness*, *Justice*, and *Truth* of God, and has become a submissive slave to the things over which he was meant to rule: which has also thrown Nature into disorder.

**C.** A continuation of the spiritual misfortunes of man since he freely opposed the *Goodness*, *Justice*, and *Truth* of God through his sin.

**CI.** Jesus Christ has merited the pardon of man’s sin on the condition of penance. <note>The author argues that while Christ "paid the debt," the benefit is only applied if the individual undergoes a process of repentance.</note>

**CII.** The opposition of men to this condition of penance. It is only by force that they endure it, even though it must be voluntary to satisfy the just will of God regarding voluntary sin.

**CIII.** In this wretched life, men seek to please and satisfy themselves, and not God.

**CIV.** God has ordained this life for man only so that he may voluntarily embrace penance, in order to enjoy His grace and finally salvation. Involuntary penance is diabolical. <note>In this context, "diabolical" refers to suffering that does not lead to redemption, similar to the eternal, unrepentant suffering of demons.</note>

**CV.** The reason for the necessity of penance comes from the JUSTICE of God, which must concur on God's part in the work of our Redemption, as well as His *Goodness* and His *Truth*, to all of which man must conform on his part. That the Holy TRINITY, incomprehensible to the human mind, can be salvifically <note>original: "salutairement"</note> conceived through these three personal and distinct properties. <note>The author appears to map the attributes of Goodness, Justice, and Truth onto the three persons of the Trinity to make the concept more accessible to the believer.</note>

**CVI.** Jesus Christ, being one with His Father, cannot but will that the man who is to be saved returns to harmony and acts himself in accordance with Divine *Justice*, which requires that one suffers through penance and converts through the EVANGELICAL LIFE. <term>Evangelical Life: A life lived strictly according to the teachings of the Gospels.</term>

**CVII.** Through a material analogy <note>original: "similitude materielle"</note> is declared the necessity of fulfilling the condition of *penance* and *conversion*, which Jesus Christ has inserted into the contract

...by which He promised man pardon and salvation through His merits.

**CVIII.** That not only the *modern applicators* <note>original: "Applicateurs modernes"; likely referring to contemporary theologians who taught that Christ's merits were applied to the soul through faith or ritual alone, without the necessity of personal moral transformation.</note> of the merits of Jesus Christ, but also the *Predestinarians*, who restrict them to specific predestined individuals, offend the JUSTICE of God.

**CIX.** In individuals, the object of God's choice is good; and the object of *Reprobation* <term>Reprobation: The theological concept of being rejected by God and destined for damnation.</term> is evil. In general, all men—considered as being in Adam, and not outside of him—equally possess *grace*, *damnation*, *pardon*, and *penance*, according to Adam's disposition: except for Jesus Christ, who was already outside of him.

**CX.** Concerning the *Primogeniture* <note>The status of being the firstborn; here, referring to Christ as the "firstborn of all creation" and the archetype for humanity.</note> of J. Christ; and how He formerly communicated with men through His glorious body.

**CXI.** Since His coming in a mortal body, J. Christ no longer communicates through His glorious body, but through His Spirit and His truth in the tranquility of the detached soul.

**CXII.** The failure of this spiritual communication with God reveals that many in the present day are false prophets.

**CXIII.** Communication with Jesus Christ is only to be found in the observance of the *Evangelical Law* <note>The moral and spiritual requirements established by the Gospel.</note>, which is the final means of our salvation.

**CXIV.** God leaves men free toward these means: but they turn away from them—both themselves and others—through wicked doctrines and actions at the prompting of the Devil.

**CXV.** One makes Jesus Christ an accomplice to sins by relying on His merits in the common fashion, while having forgotten the *fundamental truths* of the Gospel.

**CXVI.** The Father and the Son urge us to Penance.

**CXVII.** Man’s understanding being corrupted, and not knowing how to discern the penance that is pleasing and satisfying to God, Jesus Christ came to show by His example how *Christians* must perform it.

**CXVIII.** The *Jews*, through corruption of spirit, had also strayed from the goal of the Law, which was to lead them back to God through conversion of heart, and they attached themselves only to the letter and the outward appearance.

**CXIX.** God did not give the Laws for His own sake, but to remove the obstacles and inclinations that withdrew the Soul from *Divine Love*, which is the purpose of Creation.

**CXX.** Commandments, which seem impossible in the corrupted imagination: but were given to provide relief through love, and not to be an unbearable burden.

**CXXI.** That it is easier to renounce oneself than to satisfy oneself; and less difficult to take up one’s cross than to be unwilling to take it up.

**CXXII.** Necessity of observing the three *Evangelical Counsels* <term>Evangelical Counsels: In Christian theology, these are the virtues of voluntary poverty, chastity, and obedience, often seen as a path to spiritual perfection beyond the basic requirements of the law.</term>.

**CXXIII.** One cannot have the Love of God without the Evangelical Counsels.

**CXXIV.** Since the Love of God is so necessary, it is a deception to promise salvation apart from it and from *penance* <note>original: "penitence"; refers to the internal transformation and outward acts of repentance for sin.</note>, under whatever pretext it may be.

**CXXV.** No salvation nor pardon through the Merits of Jesus Christ without penance.

**CXXVI.** Jesus Christ did not wish to merit pardon or salvation for men without penance.

**CXXVII.** The example of the first Christians, and that of Jesus Christ, lead us back to penance and the love of God.

**CXXVIII.** Necessity of the mortal example of J. Christ, who was previously immortal, glorious, and the First-born of all creation.

**CXXIX.** Without sin, men would not have been subject to any infirmities, but would have been perfect, like Jesus Christ.

**CXXX.** Why it is that men do not understand the mysteries or the truths of Scripture.

**CXXXI.** There are many divine mysteries, the knowledge of which is not absolutely necessary for salvation.

**CXXXII.** Three fundamental things necessary for salvation.

**CXXXIII.** The usefulness of specific mysteries and the wonders of eternal things. The means of understanding them.

**CXXXIV.** Their indirect necessity, due to the instincts and inclinations of nature, which nature retained even after the fall.

**CXXXV.** Love for eternal things makes one embrace Life and the **Evangelical Law** <term>Evangelical Law: The moral and spiritual teachings found in the Gospels of the New Testament, presented here as the supreme guide for life.</term>.

**CXXXVI.** The Ignorant, lacking a taste and love for eternal things, have used this as a reason to blaspheme God's Laws, calling them impossible and burdensome.

**CXXXVII.** There is nothing better, richer, more honorable, or more delightful, even in this world, than the observance of the Evangelical Law, which is true virtue.

**CXXXVIII.** The eternal goods to come, which God will give to those who observe His Laws, and the blessings of creation, urge us to abandon all other affections to love Him.

**CXXXIX.** The vanity of the things to which man attaches his affections after having turned them away from God.

**CXL.** The misfortune of the man who, having abandoned the *Love of God*, has burdened his body and spirit with miseries. He will be released from these in the Resurrection.

**CXLI.** The palpable corruption of our body will not rise again; but rather the internal and immortal body which it covers, in both the good and the wicked <note>The author posits a "spiritual" or "internal" body that exists within the physical shell; it is this internal form, rather than the decaying physical matter, that experiences the resurrection.</note>.

**CXLII.** The internal body will not rise again as if it had been truly dead in itself; rather, it will shed the death and corruption with which it was covered through sin.

**CXLIII.** Nevertheless, the bodies of the wicked will forever be burdened by the sensations of the evils they caused. This will be their **Hell**.

**CXLIV.** In what sense the Scripture says that "this flesh" shall rise again.

**CXLV.** Without the Holy Spirit, one does not understand the Scripture, but instead finds fault with the truth. One must believe in Jesus Christ alone, who wishes at this time to gather and rule His people.

**CXLVI.** But men do not wish to let themselves be ruled by God, but rather by their corrupted nature, which always does evil, and which one must fight to be saved.

**CXLVII.** Men inappropriately excuse themselves from fighting their flesh, and flatter it under the pretext that it is a work of God, and that God has regard for our

**CXLVIII.** Neither the mortal corruption, under which the glorious body is invisibly hidden, nor that of the Spirit, come from God; and one must neither think of nor expect any good from them.

**CXLIX.** Whatever one says, knows, or does, if one does not renounce corruption here, it is absolutely impossible to be saved.

**CL.** Without hating one's corruption and oneself, one cannot love God.

**CLI.** Love of God is the end <note>In this context, "end" refers to the *final cause* or ultimate purpose (Latin: *finis*).</note> of our Creation.

**CLII.** Love of God and hatred of oneself, necessary for salvation.

**CLIV.** Christians, and also Jews, have so heavily glossed <term>glossed: To provide explanatory or interpretive notes. The author suggests these interpretations have obscured the core meaning of the text.</term> Scripture and the Laws of God that they have banished *Love* from them.

**CLV.** Having considered the Law without regard to *Love*, it has been judged impossible and burdensome: though it is nothing but a helpful remedy to recover Love.

**CLVI.** God is immutable <note>original: "immuable" — unchanging over time.</note> in the diversity of Laws he gives at different times: because as men fall into different evils, he unchangeably has the same will to heal them uniquely: Example in Adam, and in the Jews.

**CLVII.** One blasphemes against God by holding as burdens the things he gives us through love, and which we alone need, and not him.

**CLVIII.** The inevitable necessity of observing the Laws of God, without which salvation is hopeless: the damnable opinion that they are impossible being a fire that devours everything, without hope of reserve.

**CLIX.** That the *Love* so necessary is not found at present, even in those who desire to be Children of God.
