# Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit. Part II.

...also that you strive always to follow the *Lowliness* <note>original: "Baſſeſſe" — A key term in Bourignon’s theology, referring to the intentional choice to remain small, unimportant, and humble in the eyes of the world, mirroring the life of Christ.</note> of Jesus Christ more closely, if he is the object of your *Loves* <note>Refers to the soul's spiritual affections and devotion.</note>.

<margin>Without it, neither salvation nor virtue.</margin>
II. It is true that God gives you great Lights to discover his divine secrets, but that could not save you if, with this knowledge, you do not imitate Jesus Christ in his *Lowliness* and in his humility of heart. For even the Angels well knew the high Divine mysteries, yet with this knowledge they became Devils, because they did not follow the *Lowliness* and *Humility* of Jesus Christ. Likewise, men will perish who do not embrace and practice this *Lowliness* and humility of heart, since it is the point in which all true virtue consists.

<margin>It is rejected through Pride, ignorance, and the corruption of nature.</margin>
III. This is a truth that very few people have grasped, since today we see every person striving to take the most beautiful and the best for themselves. This bears witness to the high esteem they have for themselves, believing they deserve these estimable things, although in fact they do not deserve even the least of what God has given them. This comes from a lack of knowledge; for if they truly knew that virtue consists in always taking and choosing the least in all things, undoubtedly those who wish to become virtuous would exercise themselves in this practice—even though nature finds it repugnant, seeing as Jesus Christ has told us: *(a) that one must renounce oneself to be his disciple.* <note>Matthew 16:24: "Then Jesus said to his disciples, 'Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.'"</note>

### V.

<margin>It is better to choose the lesser things than the best,</margin>
From this it comes, My Children, that you do not well know how to resolve to always take the least of things, nor to choose the last place, according to the counsel of Jesus Christ: because your nature <note>Bourignon uses "nature" to refer to the "old man" or the fallen human state, which instinctively seeks self-preservation and status.</note> still prizes the most beautiful and the best above the lesser things. This is a blindness that the Devil has cast into your spirits, since in fact the lesser things are far more estimable, because Jesus Christ himself wished to choose them, *(b)* <note>Philippians 2:6-8: Describes Christ "emptying himself" and taking the form of a servant.</note> he to whom everything belonged, and who deserved the most beautiful and best of all things: while we know for certain that he chose the most despised things for his use. And if we wish to become his Disciples *(c)* <note>John 13:14-15: The passage where Jesus washes the disciples' feet as an example of service.</note> we must do the same with joy and satisfaction, because God does not want to be served *(d)* <note>Psalm 110:3: "Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power."</note> by constraint.

# 8th Letter: The Lowliness and Humility of Jesus Christ

<margin>Motherly toward the weak.</margin> You know that Jesus Christ your Master did this, and that I strive to imitate him in it? Although I do not do so with the perfection that I might, were I to consider your infirmity <note>Bourignon uses "infirmity" here to mean spiritual or physical frailty.</note>, which could not follow me if I sought so precisely the least in all things, as I would do if I were left to myself. For I accommodate myself to your weaknesses, just as it seems to me that God also accommodates himself to them, since he allows us to have all our necessities, indeed, in abundance.

<margin>IX. Murmurs and discontents come from the pride of life.</margin> And what brings me sorrow is to see some of you sometimes grumbling and not being content with what I do according to the Will of God. This cannot spring from humility. For the humble heart believes it always has more than it deserves in all things, and never desires more than what is strictly necessary, even judging itself unworthy of that. But when one still feels dissatisfaction at not having everything as they wish, it is a sign that the heart is still arrogant, and believes it deserves what it lacks.

<margin>X. Pride of life and self-esteem are born in the hearts of all men.</margin> And this <term>pride of life</term> <note>A reference to "the pride of life" (superbia vitae) from 1 John 2:16, often interpreted as the desire for status or self-sufficiency.</note> is hidden in the depths of the soul of all men descended from Adam: For they bring this with them at birth, because of the sin of their first common Father. They have contracted self-esteem from the malice of his sin, which Adam committed in all men when he ceased to attribute to God the glory of his being and all the perfections in which God had willed to create him, in order to attribute them to himself, as if he

### Renewal of the *Evangelical Spirit*. Part II.

...[as if he] had been its Sovereign and capable of receiving these gifts; even though he was drawn from nothingness, and was incapable of anything on his own. And this wretched self-esteem <note>In this context, "self-esteem" (estime de soi-même) refers to prideful egotism or self-importance, rather than modern self-confidence.</note> which Adam possessed was then engraved into the hearts of all the men he carried in his loins <note>A biblical way of saying "his descendants."</note>; this is why we see them all born with it. In whatever state or condition they may be, they are inclined toward self-esteem, all wanting to dominate rather than be subjected, always preferring their own feelings to those of their peers, maintaining and supporting their own imaginations as much as possible without wanting to yield to those of others, and desiring preference, seeking to have the most beautiful and the best for their own use. All these things are found in all men who live according to the impulses of their nature, just as they are also found in beasts, who always take the best for themselves when they can get it.

<margin>

Disciples of Jesus Christ must not esteem themselves.

# Second Letter.

*This letter is entirely Divine and incomparable for enlightening and convincing hearts concerning the necessity of renouncing ourselves and submitting ourselves to the will of God to live again in His Holy Spirit, in which consists the essence and the Perfection of the Christian. The means of doing so, and the reasons for leading us there—drawn sometimes from our own corruption, sometimes from the consequences of sin, from the glory and the end <note>The word "fin" here refers to the ultimate purpose or goal of human existence.</note> of our creation, from the Love of God, from present and future rewards and punishments, from the imitation of JESUS CHRIST and the Saints, from the promises of God, and others—are proposed here and there with a Light so pure <note>original: "naïve" — in the 17th century, this meant natural, simple, or unadorned.</note> and so strong, that those who wish to become Children of God cannot but be convinced in their souls that God presents to them here, through this person <note>Likely referring to the author herself, Antoinette Bourignon.</note>, the means of being birthed into Jesus Christ, and renewed in the Spirit of His Holy Gospel; and the milk of understanding which is without deceit <note>original: "laict d'intelligence qui est sans fraude" — an allusion to 1 Peter 2:2, referring to pure spiritual nourishment.</note> to nourish them there and make them grow.*

<margin>Union in the Spirit of Christ.</margin>

### Letter 2. Rebellion of the natural Spirit.

<margin>Born so as not to yield to evil.</margin> [Had I not been given] the gift of strength to resist you all, I would have undoubtedly abandoned the will of God to follow yours, in order to live in peace. For I was alone in opposing all of you, who still live according to the impulses of your corrupted nature—a nature you would have very much liked me to obey. This I could not do while remaining faithful to God. This is why I have always resisted you, and preferred not to remain your friend rather than do or say things contrary to what God was teaching me.

->VI.<-

<margin>The Spirit of God withdraws from those who do not wish to submit to it</margin> And my constancy in this matter has won the Victory, for I have obtained from God the permission to abandon you all, should you refuse to yield to the guidance of the Holy Spirit. ### Letter 2. The Spirit of God and the Spirit of Nature are Incompatible.

God forbids *taking His Name in vain* <note>Refers to the Second Commandment; the author suggests that the human "nature" naturally prefers the license of profanity or casual swearing over sacred reverence.</note>; and nature wants to have the liberty to say and swear whatever she wants. God commands to *keep the feasts holy* <note>Referring to the Sabbath and other religious holidays; in this period, these were days for strict worship rather than recreation.</note>; and nature wants then to take her frolics and pastimes. God commands to *honor Father and Mother*; nature despises them and wishes to be delivered from obedience to them. God forbids *killing*; nature always wants to take revenge on her enemies. God forbids *committing fornication* <note>Used here in the broad biblical sense of any sexual activity outside of marriage.</note>; and nature inclines toward it. God forbids *stealing*; nature always covets insatiably, and would steal what she covets, if it were not reprehensible before men. God forbids *giving false testimony*; Nature always inclines toward lying to justify herself or excuse her faults. God forbids *desiring the wife or the goods of another*; and nature always desires what she does not have that is pleasing to her, without discerning if it is another’s property. In short, nature is entirely contrary to the wills of God in all things, and can be followed in nothing by one who desires the perfection of his soul, because being entirely corrupt, she can will nothing good.

The Devil and man are equal in their fall and damnation.

Man’s damnation is eternal if he is not reborn.

The Kingdom has been prepared only for those who will have followed the designs that God had for them when creating them, which were that they would take their **delights** with God, just as God wanted to take his **delights** with men. This is, in essence, the only **WHY** God will save or damn men.

<margin>LXIII. God damns no one.</margin>
LXIII. It is not that God damns, as the ignorant imagine, since no evils can come from God. He surely saves all those who remain in his Love and take their delights with him: but all men who abandon his Love to delight in something other than God, damn themselves, by voluntarily withdrawing from the source of all good, to throw themselves into every sort of evil, consisting in the deprivation of all good; this is what is called **Hell**.

<margin>LXIV. Man’s choice. God causes salvation; neither man nor his works merit it.</margin>

### Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit. Part II.

...miserable deprivation of the glory in which God had placed man at his creation, having made him bright, agile, subtle <note>In 17th-century mystical texts, "subtle" refers to a body that is refined, ethereal, and not bound by the density of ordinary matter.</note>, and glorious—so resplendent that even on the exterior, there issued from all the pores of his body lights similar to the stars of the firmament or the rays of the Sun. Thus, this Divine body, so tender and delicate <note>Original: "deslié." Therefore, the bodies of the damned will endure the burning and the smoke of fire, the cold, the hunger, and other pains more sensitively after death than they could suffer during life—even though these evils will not be as coarse and material after death as they were during their lifetime.

Why, then, should it not have been permitted for God to create for Himself creatures with whom He wished to take His own delights? Was He not powerful enough to do so? This cannot be true: For being a perfect God, no imperfect things can come from Him. But because men, through their sins, have fallen into blindness, they see nothing except according to the reach of their short-sightedness, which cannot penetrate through the husk of our mortality to see this internal body that God has created there: looking only at the husk, they do not perceive this **glorified body** <note>original: "corps glorieux." In mystical theology, this refers to the spiritual, incorruptible body that remains pure despite the "corruption" of the physical world.</note>, which is covered beneath it, even though it is more alive and perfect than this mortal body that we see with our corrupted eyes. Although these eyes are incapable of seeing anything other than corruption, it does not follow that there is nothing else besides what we see and feel: since one finds a thousand things in nature that we neither see nor feel, even though we nevertheless know by experience that they are there. For example, in a **flint** <term>flint: "pierre de fusil," literally a "gun-stone," used historically to strike sparks and start fires</term>, we see no fire and feel no heat, and we cannot judge it to be anything other than a cold, coarse, and heavy body, without life: but by striking it, we see for certain that there is fire, life, and heat inside; for if those things were not there, they could not come out of it. It is the same with the **lodestone** <term>lodestone: "pierre d'aimant," a naturally magnetized mineral used in compasses</term>, in which one can neither see nor feel—simply by looking at or touching it—the power it has within itself to attract iron, since it is a heavy body that seems to have neither life nor vigor; yet it has within itself the force to attract iron and to turn itself of its own accord toward the North without anyone touching it. A child has nothing of his own by nature, knowing how to do nothing without the assistance of others, except to cry and to void waste from his body. Everything else is taught to him.

(1) He must be taught to eat: for if he did it by himself, he would eat dirt and all other filth he could touch, which would be greatly harmful to him.

(2) He must be taught to walk: for if he walked by himself, he would fall at the first movement of his body and would injure his head.

(3) He must be taught to speak: for if he spoke by himself, he could not make himself understood and would be of no benefit to others.

(4) He must be taught to work: for otherwise, he would spoil all the work he might do.

(5) He must finally be taught to rightly rule and govern his memory, his understanding, and all the <term>faculties of his soul: the different powers of the mind, such as will and intellect, which 17th-century thinkers believed must be disciplined</term>; or otherwise, all his vicious passions would make him insolent and unbearable to himself and to others.

# Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit. Part II.

God leads it <note>The "it" refers to the soul of the "Child of God" described in the previous section.</note>, when and as he pleases. Many suffer heavy falls because they push themselves into states or dignities—however good they may be—without being led there by God. Others walk through specific austerities or devotions, or pious enterprises, and even very painful things, in which they show themselves to be quite patient; but whenever some tribulation sent by God happens to them unexpectedly, they lament and murmur, seeing themselves deprived of their ordinary pious exercises or devotions in their own fashion.

All those people are not **Children**, but rather **grown adults** <note>original: "grandes personnes" — Bourignon uses this to describe those who are spiritually proud or self-reliant, contrasting them with the "little" child of God.</note> who want to walk by themselves; for he who is a **Child of God** does not wish to move a single step except where his Father leads him, attaching himself to nothing but what pleases Him, and suffering with **indifference** <note>In this context, "indifference" is a spiritual term meaning a state of being equally ready for whatever God ordains, whether it be comfort or suffering.</note> everything that happens to him, even if it were to come from the Devil himself. He is always dependent, content, and entirely submitted to his Father.

<margin>172. 3. One must learn to speak.</margin>
The Third condition of the Child is that he must *learn to speak*. The Child of God must believe that he knows how to say nothing good unless he learns it from his Father; and that he must always keep silent about everything that does not benefit others.

People who take pleasure in fine speeches are "big people" <note>original: "grands" — meaning those who have grown out of the humility of childhood into the vanity of the world.</note>, and often speak poorly, and no one hears them unto salvation: For they are like **sounding brass** <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 13:1, describing speech that lacks the spirit of charity.</note>, since Jesus Christ says: (*m*) <note>original: "Matth. 12. v. 36. And you will blush with shame for not having abandoned yourself to the governance of your God, who would have made you happy and wise; whereas your own inclination and will have made you miserable and restless, your passions having been the executioners and torturers of your soul. Is it not time to cease living for yourselves to return to your gentle Father, and to sacrifice your will to him by resisting your own? One must be completely out of one's senses not to do so, considering what good can come to us from it and what evil we cause by following our desires and wills. They will cause us eternal death, because they are in every way harmful to our Salvation.

# Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit. Part II.

[He] gave us all the powers of our soul, all the faculties of our body; and no one is capable of giving us a single moment of life if God does not maintain it. Does all this not oblige us to a total and absolute dependence on God? Is it not a great robbery to wish to take away from Him the authority and the governance of ourselves, to give it to our own understanding, which is nothing but darkness and ignorance? Must such a beautiful Soul allow itself to be ruled by brutal and disordered passions, to the detriment of its legitimate Lord?

<margin>178. Unspeakable cruelty against oneself when one does not wish to surrender to the rule of God.</margin>
What impiety! What barbaric injustice we commit against ourselves! What irreparable harm to continue in this well-proven Tyranny! For no one can truthfully say that they have found true contentment by following their own will; but every person must surely affirm that they have found themselves tyrannized by their own passions, and governed by their own senses. How many souls in the world lament this misfortune? And how many are there in Hell who, with desperate regret, curse the moments they began to follow their own inclinations, which led them into these eternal pains? Their misfortune is that instead of recognizing this dependence on God and giving Him what belongs to Him—absolute dominion over our understanding <note>original: "entendement," referring to the faculty of the human intellect</note>—we attribute it to ourselves, and presume to know how to govern and lead ourselves without any other dependence. Not that we declare this in words, but our actions are irreproachable witnesses to it. For we act vigorously in spirit and body to achieve our ambitions before having asked God if they are pleasing to Him or if they displease Him. It is enough that they please us for us to want to seize them by force; and if they do not succeed according to our whim, it is enough to alarm us, and cause us to murmur and despair—even to attack God sometimes, as if He were unjust or unreasonable—whereas He does all things in perfection and for our greatest utility and salvation, though the coarseness <note>original: "grossierté," meaning the dullness or limited nature of human perception</note> of our understanding judges it to be quite the opposite.

Nothing could be lacking to such a soul, thus surrendered and governed by its God, its Father. # To the Reader.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut drop cap 'I' featuring floral and scrollwork motifs.</image-desc>
It has been a long time, Friend Reader, that I have sought in my spirit to find the cause why men have thus abandoned God and the Counsels of Jesus Christ, which Christians do not follow at all, without my having been able to discover the reason for it until God made me realize that this comes from the fact that men do not know the corruption that sin has brought into their nature. They think themselves wise and good where they are foolish, ignorant, bad, and wicked. This results in them having no submission to the Law of God nor to the Gospel Doctrine <note>original: "Doctrine Evangelique," referring to the teachings found in the New Testament</note>, thinking they are wise enough for their own conduct, and that they are doing well when they are ruining everything. This belief gives them the presumption to act in all things by themselves, and not to submit to the laws of God, finding them as if unworthy of a good spirit, such as they believe they possess.

For this reason they neglect to practice the law of God and to follow the Gospel Counsels, thinking that they will surely reach salvation without the observance of these things, all the more because Scripture says *that one is not justified by the Law, and that Laws are not made for the righteous:* <note>original: "qu’on n’est pas justifié par la Loy, & que les Lois ne sont faites pour les justes," a paraphrase of themes from Galatians 2:16 and 1 Timothy 1:9</note> which is very true: For the righteous person is a law unto themselves. Furthermore, God gave no Laws to man as long as he remained in his righteousness and in his state of innocence. It was sin alone that gave rise to all the Laws; which were so necessary since the

<margin>sin</margin> <note>Catchword "peché" at the bottom of the page indicates the first word of the next page.</note>

<term>Counsels of Jesus Christ</term> — The ethical teachings and advice for spiritual perfection found in the Gospels, often distinguished from mandatory commandments.
<term>Gospel Doctrine</term> — The fundamental truths and teachings of the Christian faith as presented in the New Testament.
<term>Salvation</term> — The deliverance from sin and its consequences, believed by Christians to be brought about by faith in Christ.
<term>Righteous</term> — Morally right or justifiable; in a theological sense, someone who is in a right relationship with God.

<summary>Antoinette Bourignon addresses the reader to argue that human abandonment of God stems from a failure to recognize the inherent corruption caused by sin. She explains that while the righteous do not need laws, the fallen state of humanity makes the Law of God and the Gospel teachings essential for salvation.</summary>

It is therefore the law that saves man indirectly, since there has been no other means of salvation since the fall <note>literally "since the sin"</note> than the observance of the Laws of God: not that the Laws themselves have the power to save, but rather they are lights that reveal sins, teaching the means to amend them and recover the grace of God: And as it is written, *he who loves danger shall perish in it*; <note>A reference to the Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:27</note> so I say, that he who does not observe the Law of God remains incurable, and will never be healed of the wounds of sin; and dying in them, is damned for all eternity.

This is why a person must study themselves well to discover the misery to which sin has reduced them, and see that, after God had created them such a perfect creature, accomplished in body and spirit, full of wisdom <note>original: "sapience," a term for divine or spiritual wisdom</note> and holiness, they are now seen to be so dull and ignorant, inclined toward all sorts of evils, and subject to so many kinds of miseries of body and spirit. This cannot come from God, who never made anything evil, nor anything imperfect. All these defects and imperfections must come from a cause other than God: and there being nothing that can have power over man, it must of necessity be the free will <note><term>libre volonté: The theological concept that humans have the power to choose between good and evil; Bourignon emphasizes that this choice is the root of human suffering.</term></note> that has caused all these evils to itself, since neither Angel nor devil has a hold on man except insofar as the free will of man consents to it, and neither more nor less. # To the Reader.

<meta>The text begins mid-word, completing the thought from the previous page.</meta>

...wishing to persevere in them <note>The "them" refers to the sins or "evils of body and spirit" mentioned on the previous page.</note> and yet hoping for salvation through some way other than their own diligence. In this they are greatly mistaken, thinking that after having abandoned the Love of God by their own frank and free will, they will recover it without that same personal will; and that God, contrary to the decree He made for man to be free, will force man to do good after his sin, or save them through the merits of another <note>This is a critique of a common theological view that Christ's merits alone achieve salvation; Bourignon insists that the individual's will must also actively choose God.</note>. No, God is neither mutable nor inconstant, changing His mind as men do, who one day do what they despise the next and then repent of it. But God can repent of nothing. He willed for man to be a completely free creature whom He cannot save if the creature does not wish it. This is not because of any lack of power in God; for He shows His **Omnipotence** <term>Toute-puissance: Divine all-powerfulness, which here includes the sovereign choice to limit His own intervention in human freedom.</term> as much by not willing a thing as by willing it. Since He did not want man to be constrained in anything, man shall remain free for all eternity.

Some curious spirit might ask me whether, still having their liberty in **Hell** <term>Enfers: Referring here to the state or place of eternal separation from God.</term>, the damned could not convert themselves? I answer *No*, no more than blessed souls could still sin after death. This is not because their free will is taken away by God, but because the depraved will of the damned does not wish to **repent** <term>repentir: To turn away from sin with the intent to change.</term>, owing to the habit it has for evil, in which the personal will is resolved to persevere; and therefore it cannot convert, because it does not want to. These damned souls apply themselves instead to a frantic penance <note>In this context, "penitence enragée" refers to a state of agonizing regret or suffering that lacks the love of God, distinguishing it from holy repentance.</note>, blaspheming against God and cursing the hour of their creation, and all

<meta>catchword: the</meta>

<summary>Bourignon explains that God’s grant of free will is an eternal decree that He will not violate, meaning salvation cannot happen without a person's active desire. She further clarifies that the damned remain in Hell not because God removes their freedom, but because they have become so habituated to evil that they no longer wish to repent.</summary>
<keywords>Free Will, Salvation, Divine Omnipotence, Hell, Repentance, Human Nature, Antoinette Bourignon</keywords>

--- Page 555 ---
<meta>This page continues Antoinette Bourignon’s preface "To the Reader." On the previous page, she was discussing the persistence of free will after death and addressing whether souls in Hell could theoretically choose to leave.</meta>

# To the Reader.

...[choose to return to God? No, for they love] the things that helped or served their damnation; and thus they remain in the stubbornness of their sins for all eternity. It is just the same as with **sorcerers** <note>In the 17th century, "sorcerers" (sorciers) referred to individuals believed to have entered into explicit pacts with the Devil.</note>, who say they cannot convert, even though they still have life and the time to do penance. But they cannot because they *do not want* to leave those damnable dealings they have with the **Devil**, in which they delight by their own free and frank will. I have dealt with several of these persons, thinking to convert them to God because they made many displays of repentance. But after all my best efforts and their apparent repentance, they concluded that they did not want to leave the sensualities that the **Devil** gave them, because of the habit in which they had lived for so long. 

This seems to me the true image of the **damned souls**, who would not want to be converted even though they could, because by their own wills they delight in habitual evil. God cannot prevent this, having willed for them to be free. It is also because of this liberty that the **blessed souls** <term>Ames bien-heureuses: The "blessed" or "saints" in heaven who have achieved eternal union with God.</term> can no longer sin after death: because they do not want to. Being habituated to the good, they persevere in it for all eternity by their deliberate will, which is confirmed in **grace** <term>Grâce: Divine assistance or a state of being favored by God, which here reinforces the soul's choice to remain good.</term> so as never to want to sin again, or be unable to; because their own will is surrendered to the will of God, who can never do evil, nor allow the soul submitted to Him to sin. And although there are various names for sins, the essence of sin is nothing other than withdrawing one's affections from God to place them in something else other than Him. One places them in riches: which is called the sin of *avarice*. Another places their affections in the honor and glory of the world; which is called the sin of *pride*. Another places their affections in eating and drinking delicately <note>Original: "friamment" - suggests a greedy or refined indulgence in treats and delicacies.</note>, which is called gluttony. Another places their affections in the pleasures of the flesh: which is called the sin of *lust*: And so it is with all the other evils, which before men are called by different names, although before God there is but one sin in essence, which is to withdraw one's affections from God to place them in something else other than Him—whether it be in one's own comforts, one's intellect, one's beauty, or anything else that concerns <term>self-love: translated from the French *Amour propre*, a key 17th-century concept describing a prideful or narcissistic preoccupation with one's own interests above God's.</term> self-love.

This is what I wish to instill in the hearts of all men of good will, so that they might take the resolution to embrace an <term>Evangelical Life: a way of living based strictly on the teachings of the Gospels, usually characterized by poverty, humility, and total devotion.</term> Evangelical Life to pay the penalties due for their sins in this world, instead of paying them after death. I desire, Friend Reader, to show you through this *Third Part* in every detail what an *Evangelical Life* is, what corruption sin has brought upon man, and the necessity of overcoming this corruption before dying in order to be saved. Examine it very closely, my dear Reader, while I pray to God that He fills you with His Holy Spirit.

13. They may well let themselves be entertained by the imaginary pleasures of this life, but they can never be fully satisfied. This nature is the sworn enemy of God, for it has offended Him and thwarted the designs He had in creating us—which was solely to make Himself loved by His creature. However, the creature has voluntarily turned away from this love of God to love itself, even loving evil and *corruption*, which it effectively values more than God. It does everything it can to please and satisfy this vileness, which has caused it to lose the Kingdom of Heaven and subjected it to the suffering of eternal pains. In this, the soul is blameworthy and deserves to be hated, opposed, and confronted as the greatest enemy of our souls, whom we must always fight. For this reason, the Apostle <note>A traditional reference to Saint Paul, who frequently used the imagery of spiritual warfare and athletic struggle in his epistles (e.g., 2 Timothy 4:7).</note> says that our life is a continual combat.

Because of this, it is absolutely necessary that he practice striking down every one of these things in detail before being reborn in the grace of God. To achieve this, the Evangelical Doctrine <note>original: "Doctrine Evangelique"—the teachings of the Gospels</note> provides the means, prescribing **poverty of spirit** <term>Poverty of Spirit: A spiritual state of detachment where one recognizes their absolute dependence on God rather than material wealth or self-sufficiency.</term> against the love of riches, and the **mortification of the flesh** <term>Mortification of the flesh: The practice of self-discipline and denying physical or worldly desires to strengthen the spirit.</term> against the pleasures of this life, as when the scripture says that *flesh and blood shall not inherit the Kingdom of Heaven.* The Evangelical law also strikes against the ambition of the human mind, which always wishes to dominate and teach others; it says that *no one among Christians should be called Master*, and Jesus Christ tells his Disciples: *You call me Master, and you say well, for so I am; and yet I, who am your Master, have been the servant of all, and have washed your feet.* This overturns the glory found in dominating others and humbles the ambition of the human mind, which always wants to prefer itself over others and insists it is right in whatever it has conceived. Never act this way, my children. Rather, yield to others in things that are not evil, so that you may overcome this ambition of your spirit, which always wants to appear wise even though sin has made it foolish. This is what *corruption* <note>original: "la corruption"—referring to the fallen state of human nature</note> does not want...

# 80 Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit Part III.

...it is only necessary to follow the *inclinations of corrupted nature* <note>In 17th-century theology, "corrupted nature" refers to the human condition after the Fall, naturally inclined toward sin rather than God.</note> to be damned; nothing is more true.

69. How then is it possible that people can persuade themselves that they will become Christians while remaining attached to the love of themselves, and while seeking to satisfy their corruption, which is nothing but a stinking carrion that must soon rot in the earth and be reduced to the nothingness from which it came? Is it not unworthy of a Christian to take such care to treat well and nourish this corruption, which is an enemy of God? Would it not be better to love and treat well the work of God that is within us—this Divine soul and this glorious body that God created—rather than this vileness that sin has cast upon the work of God? It is like the rust that settles upon iron and will not depart except with force and powerful means. It is in this sense that Jesus Christ says *that the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.* <note>A reference to Matthew 11:12. Ascetic writers often interpreted this "violence" not as external force, but as the intense internal effort needed to overcome one's own vices.</note> This does not mean that one must open the gate of Paradise with cannon fire or other worldly violence, since that gate only opens through love; but corrupted nature is only overcome by force, by fighting and contradicting it. It is this nature that makes *our life a continual struggle* <note>original: "nôtre vie eſt un combat continuel." This is a common spiritual paraphrase of Job 7:1, "The life of man upon earth is a warfare."</note>: for if one does not fight it, it drags our souls to hell, depriving them of the Kingdom of Heaven. Therefore, a person is quite foolish to think they are being saved while giving their *corruption* its eases and comforts; for by doing so, that corruption strengthens itself, running like an unbridled horse toward all sorts of evils and sins without restraint.

70. But when this beastly *corruption* is resisted, it becomes submissive to reason and conforms to the will of God; not of its own accord, but through the violence that the higher part of the soul <note>In the psychology of this period, the "higher part" of the soul refers to the intellect and will, which were meant to govern the "lower" animal instincts.</note> exerts upon it. For when this corruption is tamed, it even serves the higher part of the soul. This is why it must not be killed, but rather subjected to the will of God, just as I have subjected so many people who claimed to be bound to the Devil by a specific pact. <note>In the 17th century, spiritual directors often worked with individuals who believed they had made "pacts" with the demonic; the author suggests that rigorous discipline could break such psychological or spiritual fixations.</note> I nonetheless constrained them to do the will of God in external matters; not of their own free will, but through constraint and violence, which later changed into a habit through the practice of doing good. And I see that it is exactly the same with corrupted nature when it is once overcome and conquered by the force of repeated actions that are contrary to it. It eventually yields and becomes a slave to reason, which obliges it to do everything it wants without any resistance. This is why a person can, if they wish, become a Christian by doing violence to their *corrupted nature*; for otherwise, they will never arrive there.

71. In vain does a person struggle to find the means of their salvation elsewhere than in the mortification <note><term>Mortification</term>: The practice of "killing off" one's sinful desires or ego through self-discipline or fasting to make room for spiritual growth.</note> of their *corrupted nature*. Let them observe whatever pious works and devotions they wish. These can only serve them as means to reach the love of God. But these means are not the end, any more than a boat is the port to which it is meant to carry us. If one remains forever in this boat, one will never reach dry land, being always in danger of shipwreck or of perishing in—

# V. Manner of Observing an Evangelical Life.

...a pleasant and licentious life according to the flesh, rather than a painful <note>original: "penible"; here meaning a disciplined or arduous life of spiritual effort.</note> one according to the spirit.

77. It is thus that people abuse this Sacrament of Baptism: just as they also abuse the Sanctification of the *Sabbath*, which is only observed by committing many sins: for this reason, it ought rather to be called the *day of sin* than the *day of solemnity*, seeing that on this day people commit far more sins than on other common days, when each person devotes themselves to working during the week to provide for their livelihood; whereas on Sundays they live in laziness and idleness, which breeds all kinds of sins. Pomp <note>original: "pompes"; refers to worldly vanity, status-seeking, and ostentatious display.</note>, drunkenness, lust, and gluttony find more of a place on Sundays than on other days. It is on Sunday that people go out for walks and amusement, giving free rein to their corrupt nature through debauchery and sensuality, backbiting and slandering their neighbor: such that they believe they honor God through more frequent sins on Sabbath days than on other days. To such an extent have Christians abused holy things that God now wishes to take them away from them, so that from now on He may be worshipped in Spirit and in Truth. <note>A reference to John 4:24: "God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth."</note>

...hindrance for the others, who might perhaps wish to imitate them if they did not hear me constantly scold and rebuke those who follow the *movements* of their *corrupt nature* <note>In 17th-century theology, "corrupt nature" refers to the human inclination toward sin following the Fall of Man.</note>. For even though some might have mortified <note>To "mortify" is to subdue bodily or worldly desires through self-discipline or prayer.</note> this *corruption* a little, it is nevertheless not so dead that it would not revive upon seeing objects that have not been mortified. But these blind souls, ignorant of the ways of God, are scandalized by virtue itself, and would wish for it to be formed according to the softness of their own hearts <note>original: "molesse de leur courage"; here meaning a lack of spiritual fortitude or a preference for ease.</note>, and not according to the justice of God. This justice shocks their corrupt nature, since that nature would always prefer to remain at peace—as much with evil as with good. For it is more pleasing to the senses to have rest than trouble or anger. This proceeds from the love one bears for oneself, and from the lack of charity <note>original: "charité"; here meaning "caritas," the selfless, divine love for one's neighbor's soul.</note> one has for one's neighbor in failing to rebuke their faults, which they perhaps would not recognize on their own, since the heart of man is so deceitful. 

And therefore, it is a double virtue *to be angry against evil and sin not*, as God commands <note>original: "se courroucer contre le mal & ne pas pecher"; a reference to the Latin "Irascimini, et nolite peccare" from Psalm 4:4 or Ephesians 4:26.</note>; and it is an act of charity toward one’s neighbor to prevent them from doing all the evil they would wish to do if one did not contradict them in it.

# VIII. False Renewers of the Evangelical Life

These are not signs of holiness, but rather of a completely carnal person, who has chosen her Paradise in this world, and can expect no other. I spoke with her Father, her Mother, her Sister, her brother, and her husband during my stay in Amsterdam; but she herself never came to see me. And when I asked her intimate friend the reason for this restraint, she told me that Tanneke Denys <note>Tanneke Denys (c. 1620–1683) was a Dutch visionary and follower of the spiritualist Jean de Labadie; Bourignon viewed her as a rival and a fraud.</note> did not dare come before my eyes because she had been told that I knew the interior of souls. This astonished me, and made me say that she must surely have something evil hidden within her that she feared I would discover; this was a bad omen. And as for me, I would be very glad to know of a person somewhere who knew the interior of the heart, so that they might reveal to me if there were anything evil hidden in my heart that I did not know myself, since *there is nothing more deceitful than the heart of man* <note>original: "il n'y a rien de plus trompeur que le coeur de l'homme." But these people, knowing that nothing good is within them, want to keep it hidden, and fear that another might discover it. Poor Prophets! who want to hide before men what God knows and wishes to reveal in His own time! These false Prophets and Prophetesses try in vain...

<header>VIII. False Reformers of the Evangelical Life:</header>

...had no sooner arrived at this Synod <note>original: "Synode"—Refers to the ecclesiastical assemblies of the Dutch Reformed Church which eventually condemned and deposed Jean de Labadie for his radical views and refusal to submit to church authority.</note> than he was deposed from his Parish, expelled, and forbidden from preaching there any further. This is how false Prophecies end: as was also seen in *Rothé* <note>Caspar Ruiten-Rothé (c. 1630–1702), a Dutch prophet and millenarian who predicted the end of the world and later faced legal and ecclesiastical trouble.</note>, *Tanneke Denys* <note>A Dutch visionary associated with radical spiritualist circles in the 17th century.</note>, and others of those who called themselves Prophets without it being true.

If these false Prophets harmed only their own consciences, there would not be so much damage: but when they want to prevent another from receiving the Truth of God, they do great damage to the souls of others, who through the reading of God’s truths might be converted to Him: for ignorance has caused many to perish. ### VIII. False Renewal: of the Evangelical Life

But it is in vain for them to try to maintain it when God wishes to destroy it, as He will do with all others built on sand, which the slightest storm will overturn <note>A reference to the parable of the house built on sand from Matthew 7:26–27.</note>. For it is not for men to build Churches in their own fashion. God alone must be the Founder of the True Church, and none other. It should suffice for us that Jesus Christ established the true Christian Church, without going off to divide ourselves into so many various opinions that cause schisms and disputes, each person wanting to hold their own opinion as the best, even though these are all nothing but opinions emerging from the corrupt spirits of carnal men, upon which no one should base their salvation; since there is only one God, one faith, and one true Church, which is the one that Jesus Christ built upon the earth. Therein lies the only true Church in which one can be saved. 

All other Religions cannot save, by whatever names one might wish to call them. It is not enough to be Roman <note>A reference to the Roman Catholic Church.</note>, or of Calvin, or of Luther, of Menno <note>The Mennonites, followers of Menno Simons.</note>, of Arminius <note>The Arminians, or Remonstrants, who followed the teachings of Jacobus Arminius.</note>, of the Quakers <note>original: "Trembleurs"—the literal French translation for "Quakers," referring to the Religious Society of Friends.</note>, of Labadie <note>Jean de Labadie, the leader of the community Bourignon was specifically critiquing.</note>, or other sects or Religions: all that will be nothing to our salvation. One must be a Christian, or perish eternally. 

Which all these sectaries do not sufficiently understand, thinking in their private minds that all who follow them will be saved. Always remember the conditions that true ***charity*** must have—which is ***patient***, ***kind***, and ***thinks no evil***—along with the rest of the conditions the Apostle <note>original: "l’Apôtre"; referring to Saint Paul in 1 Corinthians 13</note> described, asserting that without true charity, no one will be saved. ***Even if***, he says, ***one were to give all their goods to feed the poor, indeed, even their body to be burned; if they were to move mountains, or have the gift of Prophecy and that of performing miracles; all these virtues, along with many others, are nothing without charity.*** This is an infallible truth to which Christians pay little heed, imagining they possess charity when they have nothing but self-love. ...[you] can imitate Jesus Christ without renouncing yourselves. What is there left to interpret or dispute after that, since everything is contained in these two points: *That you cannot be Christians without imitating Jesus Christ, and that you cannot imitate Jesus Christ without renouncing yourselves?* Why do you wish to walk by four different paths <note>The phrase "marcher par quatre chemins" is a French idiom meaning to take a convoluted or indirect route instead of the straightforward one.</note> when there is only a single path that leads to life? ## X. Where evil in man comes from.

116. Some curious people might well ask how Adam was able to do evil and fall into sin, since before this he was naturally inclined toward the good, yet he actually did wrong and made himself an enemy of God? This happened because Adam, possessing his **free will** <term>free will: the power of acting without the constraint of necessity or fate; the ability to choose between different possible courses of action.</term>, did not remain within the limits of the Love he was permitted to have for creatures, but instead directed toward them the same affections that he should have reserved for God alone. By thus changing the order established by God, he greatly offended Him and lost himself along with all his posterity, for having acted directly against the designs of God. For God desired to have a creature who would love Him with all their heart so that He might take His delight with them. But in contempt of his God, man—with his **free Will**—turned those same affections he owed to God toward earthly creatures, becoming infatuated with them to the detriment of the love he owed entirely to his God. It is not that man had this evil inclination within himself to displease God; but rather that by amusing himself in considering the beauty of so many diverse creatures, they won over his heart little by little. He was in a Paradise of delights, where everything was beautiful and good in full perfection, as the works of God always are—lacking nothing, and always fully perfect and accomplished in every point. This is what ravished Adam's understanding as he admired them...

But God, wishing to have a more noble creature than all the others, willed to create man entirely free, like a **little god**, to do and to leave undone all that he willed, obliging him only to love Him as his Lord, his Creator, and his Father; everything else was left free to him. For this reason, man was made free to dominate and command them like a **little god** subject only to the **GREAT ETERNAL GOD**.

For this purpose, Scripture says before man was created: *Let us make man in our likeness.* <note>original: "Faisons un homme à nôtre semblance" — A reference to Genesis 1:26. The author uses this to argue that human dignity lies specifically in the capacity for choice.</note> And this man could not more closely resemble God than in the liberty of his will, for he could resemble God in nothing else except in this full liberty, through which he did everything he willed, since everything obeyed him. 140. It is enough that the soul follows the impulses of its corrupted nature and its own will, since that includes within itself all kinds of sins, because this self-love directly clashes with the love of God; and he who loves himself cannot love God, and he who loves God cannot love himself. This is a good sign for discerning whether a person loves God or not: For even if they were to state strongly that they love God, they lie if they still love and esteem themselves. This is why the Scripture says, *that all men are liars*, without any exception <note>original: "que tous hommes sont menteurs." A reference to Psalm 116:11, used here to suggest that man's nature is inherently deceptive when he claims to love God while still being ruled by his own ego.</note>. Many imagine that they love God when they love themselves: which is impossible; since these two loves are like heat and cold, which cannot remain together in the same subject: of necessity, one must drive out the other, the love of God being too pure to reside in a soul with the impurity of self-love.

This gives good reason for the man who wishes to become a Christian to work first of all on the foundational stone of the edifice of his virtue: true humility of heart. For otherwise, God will always resist him; even if he had acquired many other virtues, if he lacks humility, he lacks everything. It would not be enough to have conquered the *lust of the eyes* or *the lust of the flesh* if, along with these, he did not conquer *the pride of life*, which make up the three capital sins <note>These three categories—lust of the eyes, lust of the flesh, and the pride of life—come from 1 John 2:16 and represent the core of worldly temptation in Christian theology.</note> that are born with the person; and one cannot be justified <note>original: "justicié," here meaning to be made righteous or cleared of the guilt of sin.</note> without the other.

157. To be saved, one must conquer these three capital enemies, since nothing defiled shall enter the Kingdom of Heaven. Man must employ the whole time of his life in conquering, or at least in fighting, these three enemies of our souls. This is all the work he has to do in this world, which is his time of trial, where we are sent to purge our souls of the defilements that the sin of Adam brought upon them. No one can be ignorant that these three capital sins are found within the movements of our corrupt nature, and consequently that they must be fought to be saved; otherwise, we shall die as children of wrath <note>original: "enfans d’ire." This is a biblical phrase (Ephesians 2:3) referring to those who remain in their natural, fallen state under divine judgment.</note> and perdition, just as we are born. In such a case, we have no need of any other sentence of condemnation than that given to Adam, when God said to him, "*Because you have*" <note>A reference to Genesis 3:17: "Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten of the tree..." which began the fall of man.</note>

<summary>The author argues that humility is the essential foundation of Christian life, without which all other virtues and sacraments are useless. He describes human life as a period of trial dedicated to purging the soul of the three "capital sins" inherited from Adam.</summary>

->### XI. Three pillars of corruption.<-

...listened to the voice of your wife <note>This refers to the biblical account in Genesis 3:17, where God speaks to Adam after he eats the forbidden fruit.</note>, & that you have eaten of the fruit of the tree of which I had forbidden you to eat, the earth shall be cursed in you, that is to say, all the men who shall come from you will be cursed; and no one can lift man from this curse <term>curse: original French "malediction," referring to the state of being separated from God's favor following the original sin of Adam.</term> except himself: since it stems from the sin that his own will committed, this same own will must now resist this committed malignancy, or otherwise these wounds cannot be healed: for he who listens to the voice of his wife, he remains in all sorts of curses, since this corruption always disobeys God, & this cursed flesh does what God forbids to do. This is why it is necessary to resist it, and never obey what nature desires; since that is infallibly bad.

158. This is why he who does not resolve to renounce himself can never be saved, since he remains an enemy of God without reconciliation, for being born in the **Three Capital Sins**, of the *lust of the eyes*, of the *concupiscence of the flesh* <term>concupiscence: an intense worldly desire or lust, particularly those that lead away from spiritual devotion.</term>, & of the *pride of life*, which are the sources of all other sins. And instead of resisting them, one sees the **Christians** of today fostering them, increasing their desires, and the concupiscence of the flesh, and the pride of their lives. For who is there today who is content with what he has without desiring more? Who does not wish to grow greater, to be better served and treated, to amass money to better satisfy his appetite and the concupiscence of his flesh? Who does not tend

# TABLE OF CONTENTS,
## According to the Numbers of the Periods of the Book.

### I. Perversity of Corruption.

<margin>1.</margin>Subject of this Treatise. <note>original: "Traitté"</note>
<margin>2.</margin>One cannot follow the corruption of nature without doing evil.
3. We have nothing to fear but the stirrings of our own corruption.
4. Corruption inserts itself into all our affections.
5. Corruption causes one to fail to recognize salvation, the purpose of man, and even itself.
6. Only the School of Jesus Christ <note>original: "J. C."</note> cures this ignorance.
7. Men do not wish to learn there that they do nothing but evil.
8. Good works are evil when they originate from corruption.
9. One believes they love God while loving only corruption, which can provide nothing but death.

### II. Freedom to follow it, or Not:

<margin>10.</margin>Man is free to choose death or eternal life, evil or good.
11. One chooses life or death by renouncing or following corruption.
12. Few seek the Kingdom of Heaven; all seek, though in vain, the kingdom of this life.
13. Corruption causes unrest here and leads to the loss of the future life.

### III. Necessity of resolving to fight it.

<margin>14.</margin>All are damned from birth <note>Refers to the doctrine of Original Sin, suggesting humans are born in a state of separation from God.</note> if they do not immediately fight corruption to undo that damnation.
15. Man, though corrupted, will be saved by stripping away his corruption; otherwise, he will perish.
16. The merits of Jesus Christ are for those who conquer corruption by imitating Him.
17. Necessity of the Evangelical Life <note>A life lived strictly according to the teachings of the Gospels.</note> to be saved.
18. One must resolve to say *yes* or *no*, without excuses.
19. Corrupted nature does nothing but evil.

### IV. Means of overcoming Corruption.

20. Helps and obstacles to conquering corruption.

<header>Titles of the Books of Lady Antoinette Bourignon.</header>

# ANTOINETTE BOURIGNON,
## & their size.

1. The Light Born in Darkness, *in 4 parts: containing all together 53 sheets. <note>original: "feuilles." In 17th-century publishing, the number of printer's sheets was used to indicate the physical volume or length of a book, which determined the price.</note> Each part is sold separately.*
2. The Tomb of False Theology, *in 4 parts, 55 and a half sheets.*
3. Innocence Recognized, etc. 14.
4. The Light of the World, Part I, 21 sheets.
5. ---- the same, Part II, 15 sheets.
6. ---- the same, Part III, 22 sheets.
7. Warning against the Quakers. <note>original: "Trembleurs." Literally "the Shakers" or "Tremblers," a contemporary term for the Religious Society of Friends.</note> 28.
8. The Testimony of Truth, 60 *sheets*.
9. Of Solid Virtue, Part I, 17 sheets.
10. ---- the same, Part II, 22 sheets.
11. The Touchstone, 27 sheets.
12. The Blindness of Men Today, 27 and a half *sheets*.
13. Renewal of the Evangelical Spirit, Part I, 19 sheets.
14. ---- the same, Second Part, 13 sheets.
15. ---- The Third, 14 sheets.
16. The New Heaven and the New Earth, 16 and a half sheets.
17. The Academy of Learned Theologians, Part I, 13 sheets.
18. 19 --- the same, Parts II & III, *each have 10 sheets.*
20. 21. 22. The Antichrist Unmasked, <note>original: "découvert." Literally "discovered" or "uncovered," used here in the sense of revealing the true nature of the Antichrist.</note> *in 3 Parts: 30 sheets in total.*
23. The Last Mercy, 11 sheets.
24. The Holy Visor, 10 sheets.
25. The Call of God and the Refusal of Men. 11.
26. The Life of Lady *Antoinette Bourignon*. <note>original: "Damoiselle." A title of respect for an unmarried woman of noble or high social standing.</note>
27. The Stones of Jerusalem; etc. etc.
